+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Weights: cuEquivariance's parameter convention -> the kernels' layouts, once
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class TriMulWeights:
+    """The twelve parameters of the op in the kernels' layouts, prepared ONCE (:func:`prepare_weights`; a plan-time transform).
+
+    ``w_in`` ``[2, 2 c, c_z]`` = cuEquivariance's ``p_in_weight`` / ``g_in_weight`` (rows ``[a; b]``) as the substrate's two passes with the
+    value and gate rows interleaved per 128-channel block; ``b_in`` ``[2, 2 c]`` likewise (None when neither input bias was given);
+    ``b_out`` ``[2 c_z]`` = ``p_out_bias`` / ``g_out_bias`` interleaved (None when neither was given); the LayerNorm parameters and the two
+    output weights contiguous bf16.  A bias given on one side only is paired with zeros for the other -- here, at preparation, never per call.
+    """
+
+    c_z: int
+    c: int
+    w_in: torch.Tensor
+    b_in: Optional[torch.Tensor]
+    norm_in_weight: torch.Tensor
+    norm_in_bias: torch.Tensor
+    norm_out_weight: torch.Tensor
+    norm_out_bias: torch.Tensor
+    p_out_weight: torch.Tensor
+    g_out_weight: torch.Tensor
+    b_out: Optional[torch.Tensor]
+
+    @property
+    def has_in_bias(self) -> bool:
+        return self.b_in is not None
+
+    @property
+    def has_out_bias(self) -> bool:
+        return self.b_out is not None
+
+    @property
+    def device(self) -> torch.device:
+        return self.w_in.device
+
+
+#: The tensor fields of :class:`TriMulWeights`, in order -- the parameters the kernels READ (the autograd gate and the aliasing check walk them).
+_WEIGHT_FIELDS = ("w_in", "b_in", "norm_in_weight", "norm_in_bias", "norm_out_weight", "norm_out_bias", "p_out_weight", "g_out_weight", "b_out")
+
+
+def _bf16_contiguous(t: torch.Tensor, name: str, shape: Tuple[int, ...], *, cast: bool) -> torch.Tensor:
+    if tuple(t.shape) != shape:
+        raise ValueError(f"{name} must have shape {shape}, got {tuple(t.shape)}")
+    if t.dtype != torch.bfloat16:
+        if not cast:
+            raise NotImplementedError(f"{name} must be bf16 (got {t.dtype}); pass precision='bfloat16' to cast the parameters like cuEquivariance does")
+        t = t.to(torch.bfloat16)
+    return t.contiguous()
+
+
+def prepare_weights(
+    norm_in_weight: torch.Tensor,
+    norm_in_bias: torch.Tensor,
+    p_in_weight: torch.Tensor,
+    p_in_bias: Optional[torch.Tensor],
+    g_in_weight: torch.Tensor,
+    g_in_bias: Optional[torch.Tensor],
+    norm_out_weight: torch.Tensor,
+    norm_out_bias: torch.Tensor,
+    p_out_weight: torch.Tensor,
+    p_out_bias: Optional[torch.Tensor],
+    g_out_weight: torch.Tensor,
+    g_out_bias: Optional[torch.Tensor],
+    *,
+    cast_to_bf16: bool = False,
+) -> TriMulWeights:
+    """cuEquivariance's parameters (``p_in_weight``, ``g_in_weight`` ``[2 c, c_z]`` rows ``[a; b]``; ``p_out_weight`` ``[c_z, c]``;
+    ``g_out_weight`` ``[c_z, c_z]``; LayerNorm vectors ``[c_z]`` / ``[c]``; biases optional) -> :class:`TriMulWeights`.  Copies (the
+    interleaves), so call it once per parameter set; ``cast_to_bf16`` casts wider parameters (cuEquivariance's ``precision='bfloat16'``)."""
+    for name, w in (("norm_in_weight", norm_in_weight), ("norm_in_bias", norm_in_bias), ("p_in_weight", p_in_weight), ("g_in_weight", g_in_weight)):
+        if w is None:
+            raise ValueError(f"{name} is required (this API never initialises parameters implicitly)")
+    for name, w in (("norm_out_weight", norm_out_weight), ("norm_out_bias", norm_out_bias), ("p_out_weight", p_out_weight), ("g_out_weight", g_out_weight)):
+        if w is None:
+            raise ValueError(f"{name} is required (this API never initialises parameters implicitly)")
+    if p_in_weight.ndim != 2 or p_in_weight.shape[0] % 2:
+        raise ValueError(f"p_in_weight must be [2 c, c_z] (rows [a; b]), got {tuple(p_in_weight.shape)}")
+    c = int(p_in_weight.shape[0]) // 2
+    c_z = int(p_in_weight.shape[1])
+    bf = lambda t, n, shp: _bf16_contiguous(t, n, shp, cast=cast_to_bf16)  # noqa: E731
+    p_in = bf(p_in_weight, "p_in_weight", (2 * c, c_z))
+    g_in = bf(g_in_weight, "g_in_weight", (2 * c, c_z))
+    ln_in_w = bf(norm_in_weight, "norm_in_weight", (c_z,))
+    ln_in_b = bf(norm_in_bias, "norm_in_bias", (c_z,))
+    ln_out_w = bf(norm_out_weight, "norm_out_weight", (c,))
+    ln_out_b = bf(norm_out_bias, "norm_out_bias", (c,))
+    p_out = bf(p_out_weight, "p_out_weight", (c_z, c))
+    g_out = bf(g_out_weight, "g_out_weight", (c_z, c_z))
+    dev = p_in.device
+    if p_in_bias is not None or g_in_bias is not None:
+        pb = bf(p_in_bias, "p_in_bias", (2 * c,)) if p_in_bias is not None else torch.zeros(2 * c, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device=dev)
+        gb = bf(g_in_bias, "g_in_bias", (2 * c,)) if g_in_bias is not None else torch.zeros(2 * c, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device=dev)
+        b_in = k1.stack_projection_biases(pb, gb)
+    else:
+        b_in = None
+    if p_out_bias is not None or g_out_bias is not None:
+        pob = bf(p_out_bias, "p_out_bias", (c_z,)) if p_out_bias is not None else torch.zeros(c_z, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device=dev)
+        gob = bf(g_out_bias, "g_out_bias", (c_z,)) if g_out_bias is not None else torch.zeros(c_z, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device=dev)
+        b_out = k3.stack_tail_biases(pob, gob)
+    else:
+        b_out = None
+    return TriMulWeights(
+        c_z=c_z,
+        c=c,
+        w_in=k1.stack_projection_weights(p_in, g_in),
+        b_in=b_in,
+        norm_in_weight=ln_in_w,
+        norm_in_bias=ln_in_b,
+        norm_out_weight=ln_out_w,
+        norm_out_bias=ln_out_b,
+        p_out_weight=p_out,
+        g_out_weight=g_out,
+        b_out=b_out,
+    )
+
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# The prepared API
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+class TriangleMultiplicativeUpdateFwd(APIBase):
+    """Triangle multiplicative update, forward: one declaration, one workspace, three launches on one stream.
+
+    Declaration (the constructor): the pair representation's shape and dtype (``sample_x`` ``[B, N, N, c_z]`` bf16, a tensor or a
+    :class:`cudnn.api_base.TensorDesc`), the ``direction``, the hidden width ``c_hidden`` (= ``p_in_weight.shape[0] // 2``) and the
+    optional-tensor flags ``has_mask`` / ``has_in_bias`` / ``has_out_bias`` -- compile-time specialisations the execute arguments must match
+    exactly (a mask handed to a plan compiled without one raises; so does a missing mask on a plan compiled with one).  ``k2_tile`` names
+    a FROST GEMM tile config for the contraction instead of the measured per-geometry pick, ``knobs`` a :class:`heuristics.TriMulKnobs` whose
+    SET axes override the measured pick for this geometry (an axis left ``None`` keeps the table's value: ``TriMulKnobs(clc_stages=4)`` changes
+    the ring depth only).  Performance only; every member of every domain computes the same function; the vocabulary is validated by
+    ``check_support``, the contraction tile's eligibility for this geometry probed there without a compile.
+
+    ``check_support`` raises the typed declines listed in the module docstring, ``compile`` builds the three plans (cached per
+    parameter set across instances), ``get_workspace_size`` is the planes + ``y`` carve, ``execute(x, mask, weights, out, workspace)``
+    validates (dtype, shape, contiguity, alignment, flag agreement) and launches K1, K2, K3 on ``current_stream`` (None = torch's current
+    stream).  No allocation, conversion or synchronisation on the execute path: a captured CUDA graph replays it.
+    """
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        sample_x,
+        direction: str = "outgoing",
+        *,
+        c_hidden: int,
+        has_mask: bool = True,
+        has_in_bias: bool = False,
+        has_out_bias: bool = False,
+        eps: float = 1e-5,
+        k2_tile: Optional[str] = None,
+        knobs: Optional[th.TriMulKnobs] = None,
+    ):
+        super().__init__()
+        self._warn_experimental_api()
+        if direction not in DIRECTIONS:
+            raise ValueError(f"direction must be one of {DIRECTIONS}, got {direction!r}")
+        shape, dtype, device = _shape_dtype_device(sample_x, "sample_x")
+        if len(shape) == 3:
+            shape = (1,) + shape
+        if len(shape) != 4 or shape[1] != shape[2]:
+            raise ValueError(f"sample_x must be [B, N, N, c_z] (or [N, N, c_z]), got {shape}")
+        self.batch, self.n_res, _, self.c_z = shape
+        self.c = int(c_hidden)
+        self.direction = direction
+        self.dtype = dtype
+        self.device = torch.device(device)
+        self.has_mask = bool(has_mask)
+        self.has_in_bias = bool(has_in_bias)
+        self.has_out_bias = bool(has_out_bias)
+        self.eps = float(eps)
+        # the performance knobs: the measured defaults for this geometry (heuristics.recommend: width, N bucket, batch bucket, direction), the
+        # caller's knobs (its set axes) / k2_tile over them -- always a complete record; the vocabulary is checked in check_support (ValueError),
+        # the contraction tile's eligibility probed there (NotImplementedError)
+        # the device's compute capability, read here so the heuristics' arch column follows the part the plan is declared on (None when no
+        # CUDA device can be asked: the Rubin table; check_support then declines the device before any launch); the substrate body is
+        # resolved in check_support (``self.arch``)
+        self.cc = self._device_cc()
+        self.arch: Optional[str] = None
+        self.knobs = th.resolve(self.n_res, self.c, self.batch, direction, k2_tile=k2_tile, knobs=knobs, cc=self.cc)
+        self.k2_tile = self.knobs.k2_tile
+        self.n_pad = k2.n_pad(self.n_res)
+        self._plan_k1 = None
+        self._plan_k3 = None
+        self._k2 = None
+        self._k2_binding = None
+
+    def _device_cc(self) -> Optional[Tuple[int, int]]:
+        """The declaration device's compute capability, or None when it cannot be read here (a non-CUDA declaration, no CUDA runtime)."""
+        if self.device.type != "cuda" or not torch.cuda.is_available():
+            return None
+        try:
+            return tuple(int(x) for x in torch.cuda.get_device_capability(self.device_index))
+        except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 -- an unreadable device is check_support's typed decline, not the constructor's
+            return None
+
+    # -- declaration checks -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+    def check_support(self) -> bool:
+        """Typed declines, malformed declarations first (``ValueError``), then the serving envelope and the arch (``NotImplementedError``)."""
+        b, n, c_z, c = self.batch, self.n_res, self.c_z, self.c
+        if b < 1 or n < 1:
+            raise ValueError(f"x must have B >= 1 and N >= 1, got B={b}, N={n}")
+        if c_z % HIDDEN_DIM_MULTIPLE:
+            raise ValueError(f"the pair width c_z must be a multiple of {HIDDEN_DIM_MULTIPLE}, got {c_z}")
+        if c < 1 or c % HIDDEN_DIM_MULTIPLE:
+            raise ValueError(f"the hidden width c (= p_in_weight.shape[0] // 2) must be a positive multiple of {HIDDEN_DIM_MULTIPLE}, got {c}")
+        if not (self.eps > 0.0):
+            raise ValueError(f"eps must be > 0, got {self.eps}")
+        th.validate_knobs(self.knobs)  # an out-of-vocabulary tile-config name / tile order / ring depth is a malformed declaration
+        if self.dtype != torch.bfloat16:
+            raise NotImplementedError(f"triangle_multiplicative_update serves bf16 pair representations only, got {self.dtype}")
+        if c_z not in SUPPORTED_CHANNELS:
+            raise NotImplementedError(
+                f"triangle_multiplicative_update serves c_z in {SUPPORTED_CHANNELS} today (the LayerNorm-prologue GEMM substrate's widths), got c_z={c_z}"
+            )
+        if c != c_z:
+            raise NotImplementedError(
+                f"triangle_multiplicative_update serves c_hidden == c_z today (one K for the output gate and projection GEMMs), got c_hidden={c}, c_z={c_z}"
+            )
+        if n < MIN_N_RES:
+            raise NotImplementedError(f"triangle_multiplicative_update needs N >= {MIN_N_RES} (the output stage's 64-row MN-major TMA box), got N={n}")
+        if self.direction == "incoming" and not k2.incoming_supported(n):
+            raise NotImplementedError(
+                f"the incoming direction needs N % {k2.CONTIGUOUS_EXTENT_MULTIPLE} == 0 today (the contraction reads MN-major operands whose contiguous "
+                f"extent is N, and a TMA-fed contiguous extent must be a multiple of 8 bf16 elements), got N={n}"
+            )
+        if b * n * n * c_z >= _INT32_MAX or 2 * c * b * n * self.n_pad >= _INT32_MAX:
+            raise NotImplementedError(
+                f"triangle_multiplicative_update addresses its tensors with 32-bit element offsets: B*N*N*c_z = {b * n * n * c_z} and the planes' "
+                f"2*c*B*N*n_pad = {2 * c * b * n * self.n_pad} must both stay below 2^31 = {_INT32_MAX}"
+            )
+        if self.device.type != "cuda":
+            raise ValueError(f"x must be a CUDA tensor, got device {self.device}")
+        index = self.device_index
+        cc = tuple(int(x) for x in torch.cuda.get_device_capability(index))
+        if cc not in _ARCHS_BY_CC:
+            served = ", ".join(f"{a}.{b}" for a, b in _SERVED_CCS)
+            raise NotImplementedError(
+                f"triangle_multiplicative_update is rendered for compute capabilities {served} (Blackwell SM100 / SM103, Rubin SM107) only today; found {cc[0]}.{cc[1]}"
+            )
+        self.cc = cc
+        self.arch = _body_arch_for_cc(cc)
+        # the two LayerNorm-prologue stages' records, validated against the BODY this device runs (the substrate's typed declines -- the per-arch K
+        # cap, the sm100 register-form class ptxas cannot allocate -- fire HERE, never inside compile()): a knob set the arch cannot serve is a
+        # NotImplementedError of this declaration, a malformed one stays the substrate's ValueError
+        from cudnn.gemm.frost.ln_prologue import validate_ln_dual_gemm_params as _validate_substrate
+
+        for stage_params in self._stage_params():
+            try:
+                _validate_substrate(stage_params, self.arch)
+            except ValueError as error:
+                raise NotImplementedError(
+                    f"triangle_multiplicative_update cannot serve this knob set on compute capability {cc[0]}.{cc[1]}: {error}"
+                ) from error
+        msg = cutedsl_requirement_error("triangle_multiplicative_update")
+        if msg:
+            raise NotImplementedError(msg)
+        msg = cutedsl_arch_requirement_error(cc)
+        if msg:
+            raise NotImplementedError(msg)
+        self._probe_contraction_tile()
+        self._is_supported = True
+        return True
+
+    def _probe_contraction_tile(self) -> None:
+        """The contraction tile's eligibility for THIS geometry on THIS device without a ``cute.compile`` (the FROST GEMM engine's own
+        ``check_support`` gates over the direction's operand majors, the folded ``c * B`` batch and the arch): a catalog name the engine
+        cannot run here is a typed ``NotImplementedError`` from ``check_support``, never a bare error inside ``compile()``."""
+        import cudnn
+        import cudnn.gemm.frost  # noqa: F401  -- the pygraph recorder hook the GEMM analyzer reads
+        from cudnn.gemm.frost.sm100.compiler import probe_supported
+        from cudnn.gemm.frost.tile_config import by_name
+
+        graph = k2.contraction_graph(cudnn, self.c, self.n_res, self.direction, batch=self.batch, padded=True)
+        try:
+            with torch.cuda.device(self.device_index):
+                probe_supported(graph, by_name(self.k2_tile))
+        except NotImplementedError:
+            raise
+        except Exception as error:  # the engine's untyped refusals (a synthesized name's geometry, a template gate) become the typed decline
+            raise NotImplementedError(
+                f"the contraction tile config {self.k2_tile!r} cannot serve the {self.direction} contraction at N={self.n_res}, c={self.c}, B={self.batch} "
+                f"on this device: {type(error).__name__}: {error}"
+            ) from error
+
+    @property
+    def device_index(self) -> int:
+        """The declaration's CUDA device index (``torch.cuda.current_device()`` when the declaration named ``cuda`` without an index)."""
+        return self.device.index if self.device.index is not None else torch.cuda.current_device()
+
+    # -- workspace ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+    @property
+    def planes_shape(self) -> Tuple[int, int, int, int]:
+        return k1.planes_shape(self.c, self.batch, self.n_res)
+
+    @property
+    def y_shape(self) -> Tuple[int, int, int]:
+        return k3.y_shape(self.c, self.batch, self.n_res)
+
+    def _planes_bytes(self) -> int:
+        p = self.planes_shape
+        return _align_up(2 * p[0] * p[1] * p[2] * p[3])
+
+    def _y_bytes(self) -> int:
+        y = self.y_shape
+        return _align_up(2 * y[0] * y[1] * y[2])
+
+    def _slack_bytes(self) -> int:
+        """The readable tail after the ``b`` plane the outgoing contraction over-reads at ``N % 8 != 0`` (:func:`k2.k2_slack_bytes`)."""
+        return _align_up(k2.k2_slack_bytes(self.n_res)) if self.direction == "outgoing" else 0
+
+    def get_workspace_size(self) -> int:
+        """Bytes of the one workspace ``execute`` carves: the two channel-major planes ``a``, ``b`` (plus the contraction's over-read slack
+        at ``N % 8 != 0``) and the contraction output ``y`` (bf16, the inner axis padded to a multiple of 8), each 256-byte aligned."""
+        return self._planes_bytes() + self._slack_bytes() + self._y_bytes()
+
+    def traffic_bytes(self) -> int:
+        """The compulsory HBM traffic model of one call: ``18 N^2 C`` bytes per batch entry plus the mask (2 B per pair) -- read against the
+        measured figure in the documentation."""
+        return (
+            k1.proj_bytes(self.c_z, self.c, self.batch, self.n_res, with_mask=self.has_mask, with_stats=False)
+            + k2.contraction_bytes(self.c, self.n_res, batch=self.batch)
+            + k3.tail_bytes(self.c_z, self.c, self.batch, self.n_res, with_stats=False)
+        )
+
+    def flop(self) -> int:
+        return (
+            k1.proj_flop(self.c_z, self.c, self.batch, self.n_res)
+            + k2.contraction_flop(self.c, self.n_res, batch=self.batch)
+            + k3.tail_flop(self.c_z, self.c, self.batch, self.n_res)
+        )
+
+    # -- compile ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+    def _k3_ln_pass_form(self) -> str:
+        # the re-read LayerNorm forms re-read the MN-major operand in every pass, which the transpose prologue's K-major writes would overwrite
+        # (a typed decline of the substrate): under `transpose` the output stage keeps the register form and the knob's value serves the
+        # projection stage alone
+        return self.knobs.ln_pass_form if self.knobs.k3_prologue == "mn_major" else "registers"
+
+    def _k3_ln_once(self) -> str:
+        """The output stage's LayerNorm-once work item: the knob's value where the item spans at least two GEMM tiles there (one pass, so
+        ``"block"`` at two N tiles = c = 256), else today's per-tile item -- the substrate declines a one-tile item (K3 at c = 128; ``"passes"``
+        under one pass), so the knob's value serves the projection stage alone on those plans.  GPU-free (pinned by the API tests)."""
+        form = self.knobs.ln_once or ""
+        if not form:
+            return ""
+        trial = k3.tail_params(self.c_z, self.c, has_bias=self.has_out_bias, want_stats=False, a0_prologue=self.knobs.k3_prologue, ln_once=form)
+        return form if _ln_once_tiles_per_item(trial) >= 2 else ""
+
+    def _register_split_hints(self) -> Tuple[int, int]:
+        """The `.minnctapersm` launch hint of (K1, K3): the caller's `min_blocks_per_mp` override for both stages, else the per-RENDERING rule with
+        each stage's own bias flag, LayerNorm form, (K1) tile order and LayerNorm work item (`heuristics.register_split_hint`: whether a rendering
+        spills at the flat allocation is a property of the rendering, not of the geometry -- and the LayerNorm-once item's rendering spills UNDER
+        the hint where the per-tile item's did without it, so the rows name the per-tile item); the width is the heuristics' (`c`, = `c_z` on every
+        served plan).  GPU-free (pinned by the API tests)."""
+        hint = self.knobs.min_blocks_per_mp
+        if hint is not None:
+            return int(hint), int(hint)
+        return (
+            th.register_split_hint(
+                "k1", self.c, self.has_in_bias, self.knobs.ln_pass_form, self.knobs.epi_math, self.knobs.k1_pass_order, self.knobs.ln_once or "", cc=self.cc
+            ),
+            th.register_split_hint("k3", self.c, self.has_out_bias, self._k3_ln_pass_form(), self.knobs.epi_math, None, self._k3_ln_once(), cc=self.cc),
+        )
+
+    def _stage_params(self):
+        """The (K1, K3) substrate records this declaration compiles -- ONE builder for ``check_support`` (validated against the arch body) and
+        ``compile`` (built), so a decline and a build can never disagree on the record.  GPU-free."""
+        k3_ln_pass_form = self._k3_ln_pass_form()
+        k1_hint, k3_hint = self._register_split_hints()
+        k1_ln_once, k3_ln_once = self.knobs.ln_once or "", self._k3_ln_once()
+        return (
+            k1.proj_params(
+                self.c_z,
+                self.c,
+                has_bias=self.has_in_bias,
+                has_mask=self.has_mask,
+                want_stats=False,
+                eps=self.eps,
+                pass_order=self.knobs.k1_pass_order,
+                clc_stages=self.knobs.clc_stages,
+                ln_pass_form=self.knobs.ln_pass_form,
+                epi_math=self.knobs.epi_math,
+                min_blocks_per_mp=k1_hint,
+                ln_once=k1_ln_once,
+                ln_once_b_stages=(self.knobs.ln_once_b_stages or 0) if k1_ln_once else 0,
+            ),
+            k3.tail_params(
+                self.c_z,
+                self.c,
+                has_bias=self.has_out_bias,
+                want_stats=False,
+                eps=self.eps,
+                a0_prologue=self.knobs.k3_prologue,
+                clc_stages=self.knobs.clc_stages,
+                ln_pass_form=k3_ln_pass_form,
+                epi_math=self.knobs.epi_math,
+                min_blocks_per_mp=k3_hint,
+                ln_once=k3_ln_once,
+                ln_once_b_stages=(self.knobs.ln_once_b_stages or 0) if k3_ln_once else 0,
+            ),
+        )
+
+    def compile(self) -> None:
+        """Build the three plans: K1 (the columns arm of the substrate), K2 (the FROST GEMM engine's dense template for the per-N tile over the
+        folded ``c * B`` batch), K3 (the accumulators arm).  Each is cached on its parameter set; a second instance of the same declaration
+        reuses them."""
+        self._ensure_support_checked()
+        import cudnn
+        import cudnn.gemm.frost  # noqa: F401  -- installs the pygraph recorder hook the GEMM compiler reads
+
+        # Compile and load on the PLAN's device: the declaration may name a device other than torch's current one (a multi-GPU host with
+        # ``x`` on ``cuda:1``).  A compiled launchable is bound to the context it was loaded in, so K1 / K3 and K2 are cached per
+        # (parameter set, arch body, device) -- :func:`_substrate_plan_on`, :func:`_compile_contraction`.
+        k1_params, k3_params = self._stage_params()
+        arch = self.arch if self.arch is not None else _body_arch_for_cc(self.cc)
+        with torch.cuda.device(self.device_index):
+            self._plan_k1 = _substrate_plan_on(k1.build_trimul_proj, k1_params, self.device_index, arch)
+            self._plan_k3 = _substrate_plan_on(k3.build_trimul_tail, k3_params, self.device_index, arch)
+            self._k2 = _compile_contraction(cudnn, self.c, self.batch, self.n_res, self.direction, self.k2_tile, self.device_index)
+        self._k2_binding = self._k2.binding
+        self._compiled_kernel = (self._plan_k1, self._k2, self._plan_k3)
+
+    # -- execute ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+    def _check_execute_args(self, x, mask, weights, out, workspace) -> None:
+        b, n, c_z, c = self.batch, self.n_res, self.c_z, self.c
+        bf16 = torch.bfloat16
+        if isinstance(weights, TriMulWeights):
+            _autograd_decline([("x", x), ("mask", mask), ("out", out)] + [(f"weights.{f}", getattr(weights, f)) for f in _WEIGHT_FIELDS])
+        else:
+            _autograd_decline([("x", x), ("mask", mask), ("out", out)])
+        # the PLAN's device first: its kernels are loaded on cuda:<device_index> and launched there -- tensors on another device would pass
+        # every shape check below and hand foreign pointers to kernels running on the wrong GPU
+        if self.device.type == "cuda" and (not isinstance(x, torch.Tensor) or x.device.type != "cuda" or x.device.index != self.device_index):
+            raise ValueError(
+                f"x lives on {getattr(x, 'device', None)}; this plan was declared on cuda:{self.device_index} and its kernels are loaded there "
+                "(declare and compile one plan per device)"
+            )
+        if not isinstance(x, torch.Tensor) or x.dtype != bf16 or not x.is_contiguous() or tuple(x.shape) != (b, n, n, c_z):
+            raise ValueError(
+                f"x must be a contiguous bf16 [{b}, {n}, {n}, {c_z}] tensor (the declaration), got {getattr(x, 'shape', None)} {getattr(x, 'dtype', None)}"
+            )
+        if not isinstance(out, torch.Tensor) or out.dtype != bf16 or not out.is_contiguous() or tuple(out.shape) != (b, n, n, c_z):
+            raise ValueError(f"out must be a contiguous bf16 [{b}, {n}, {n}, {c_z}] tensor, got {getattr(out, 'shape', None)} {getattr(out, 'dtype', None)}")
+        if self.has_mask:
+            if mask is None:
+                raise ValueError("this plan was compiled with has_mask=True; a bf16 [B, N, N] mask must be passed (no silent all-valid fallback)")
+            if mask.dtype != bf16 or not mask.is_contiguous() or tuple(mask.shape) != (b, n, n):
+                raise ValueError(f"mask must be a contiguous bf16 [{b}, {n}, {n}] tensor, got {tuple(mask.shape)} {mask.dtype}")
+        elif mask is not None:
+            raise ValueError("this plan was compiled with has_mask=False; mask must be None (compile a plan with has_mask=True to apply one)")
+        if not isinstance(weights, TriMulWeights):
+            raise TypeError("weights must be a TriMulWeights (prepare_weights(...)); the kernels take the interleaved layouts, prepared once")
+        if (weights.c_z, weights.c) != (c_z, c):
+            raise ValueError(f"weights were prepared for (c_z, c) = {(weights.c_z, weights.c)}, the plan for {(c_z, c)}")
+        if weights.has_in_bias != self.has_in_bias:
+            raise ValueError(f"this plan was compiled with has_in_bias={self.has_in_bias}; the weights carry an input bias: {weights.has_in_bias}")
+        if weights.has_out_bias != self.has_out_bias:
+            raise ValueError(f"this plan was compiled with has_out_bias={self.has_out_bias}; the weights carry an output bias: {weights.has_out_bias}")
+        if (
+            not isinstance(workspace, torch.Tensor)
+            or workspace.dtype != torch.uint8
+            or workspace.numel() < self.get_workspace_size()
+            or not workspace.is_contiguous()
+        ):
+            raise ValueError(f"workspace must be a contiguous uint8 tensor of at least get_workspace_size() = {self.get_workspace_size()} bytes")
+        for name, t in (("x", x), ("out", out), ("workspace", workspace), ("mask", mask)):
+            if t is not None and t.device != x.device:
+                raise ValueError(f"{name} must live on x's device {x.device}, got {t.device}")
+        if weights.device != x.device:
+            raise ValueError(f"weights must live on x's device {x.device}, got {weights.device}")
+        if workspace.data_ptr() % _WS_ALIGN:
+            raise ValueError(f"workspace must be {_WS_ALIGN}-byte aligned")
+        # The buffers the kernels WRITE -- `out` (the output stage, while it reads x) and the workspace (the projection stage's planes while x,
+        # the mask and the parameters are read; the contraction's y) -- must not intersect any buffer they READ, nor each other, as BYTE RANGES:
+        # pointer equality is not that test.  An `out` view starting inside x (two views over one allocation) has a distinct data_ptr, and the
+        # output stage overwrote rows of x it had still to read (measured at N = 512: 16.7 M differing elements, max |diff| 2.56; smaller N and
+        # offsets happened to pass).  A typed ValueError naming both operands, before any launch (the parameters may overlap each other).
+        check_buffers_disjoint(
+            (("out", out), ("workspace", workspace)),
+            [("x", x), ("mask", mask)] + [(f"weights.{f}", getattr(weights, f)) for f in _WEIGHT_FIELDS],
+        )
+
+    def _carve(self, workspace: torch.Tensor):
+        """``(plane_a, plane_b, y)`` views over the workspace (no allocation)."""
+        p = self.planes_shape
+        planes = workspace[: 2 * p[0] * p[1] * p[2] * p[3]].view(torch.bfloat16).view(*p)
+        yb = self._y_bytes()
+        y_off = self._planes_bytes() + self._slack_bytes()
+        y = workspace[y_off : y_off + yb][: 2 * self.y_shape[0] * self.y_shape[1] * self.y_shape[2]].view(torch.bfloat16).view(*self.y_shape)
+        return planes, planes[0], planes[1], y
+
+    def execute(self, x, mask, weights, out, workspace, current_stream: Optional[cuda.CUstream] = None) -> None:
+        """Launch K1, K2, K3 on ``current_stream`` (None = torch's current stream on the plan's device).  Validates, never converts or
+        allocates.  The launches run with the plan's device current (``torch.cuda.device`` -- a context switch, no synchronisation), so a
+        plan declared on ``cuda:1`` is served from any current device."""
+        if self._compiled_kernel is None:
+            raise RuntimeError("compile() must run before execute()")
+        self._check_execute_args(x, mask, weights, out, workspace)
+        stream = _stream_handle(current_stream, self.device)
+        with torch.cuda.device(self.device_index):
+            self._launch(x, mask, weights, out, workspace, stream)
+
+    def _launch(self, x, mask, weights, out, workspace, stream: int) -> None:
+        planes, plane_a, plane_b, y = self._carve(workspace)
+        b, n, c_z = self.batch, self.n_res, self.c_z
+        k1.run_trimul_proj(
+            self._plan_k1,
+            x,
+            weights.w_in,
+            planes,
+            weights.norm_in_weight,
+            weights.norm_in_bias,
+            bias_stacked=weights.b_in,
+            mask=mask,
+            stats=None,
+            stream=stream,
+            k_block=self.knobs.k_block,
+        )
+        a_v, b_v, y_v = k2.k2_operand_views(plane_a, plane_b, y, channels=self.c, batch=b, n_res=n, direction=self.direction)
+        bd = self._k2_binding
+        self._k2({bd.a_operands[0]: a_v, bd.b_operands[0]: b_v, bd.outputs[0]: y_v}, stream=stream)
+        k3.run_trimul_tail(
+            self._plan_k3,
+            y,
+            x,
+            weights.p_out_weight,
+            weights.g_out_weight,
+            out,
+            weights.norm_out_weight,
+            weights.norm_out_bias,
+            weights.norm_in_weight,
+            weights.norm_in_bias,
+            biases=weights.b_out,
+            stats=None,
+            residual=None,
+            stream=stream,
+            k_block=self.knobs.k_block,
+        )
+
+    def make_cuda_graph(self, x, mask, weights, out, workspace, *, warmup: int = 2) -> "torch.cuda.CUDAGraph":
+        """Capture the three launches for THESE buffers into one ``torch.cuda.CUDAGraph`` (replay = one graph launch per call; the
+        buffers' contents may change between replays, their addresses may not).  ``warmup`` eager calls run first on a side stream."""
+        side = torch.cuda.Stream(device=x.device)
+        side.wait_stream(torch.cuda.current_stream(x.device))
+        with torch.cuda.stream(side):
+            for _ in range(int(warmup)):
+                self.execute(x, mask, weights, out, workspace, current_stream=cuda.CUstream(side.cuda_stream))
+        torch.cuda.current_stream(x.device).wait_stream(side)
+        torch.cuda.synchronize(x.device)
+        graph = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
+        with torch.cuda.graph(graph, stream=side):
+            self.execute(x, mask, weights, out, workspace, current_stream=cuda.CUstream(side.cuda_stream))
+        return graph
+
+
+_K2_LOCK = threading.Lock()
+_K2_CACHE: Dict[Tuple[Any, ...], Any] = {}
+_SUBSTRATE_LOCK = threading.Lock()
+_SUBSTRATE_PLANS: Dict[Tuple[Any, int], Any] = {}
+
+
+def _substrate_plan_on(build, params, device_index: int, arch: str = "sm107"):
+    """One cute-compiled launchable of the K1 / K3 substrate per (parameter set, arch body, device).  A CuTe-DSL launchable is bound to the CUDA
+    context it was first loaded in -- a K1 launchable built on ``cuda:0`` fails on ``cuda:1`` with ``cudaErrorInvalidValue`` at launch, and
+    vice versa (measured on a two-GPU host) -- while the substrate's ``build_*`` cache is per parameter set only.  Under the plan's device:
+    when the substrate's cache fills NOW its launchable is bound here and is reused (the single-device case pays nothing extra); when it was
+    filled earlier -- by a plan on another device, or by a caller outside this API -- the same template module gets a second ``cute.compile``
+    for this device, cached per (params, device)."""
+    from cudnn.gemm.frost import ln_prologue
+
+    key = (params, str(arch), int(device_index))
+    with _SUBSTRATE_LOCK:
+        hit = _SUBSTRATE_PLANS.get(key)
+    if hit is not None:
+        return hit
+    with torch.cuda.device(device_index), _SUBSTRATE_LOCK:
+        before = ln_prologue.build_ln_dual_gemm.cache_info().currsize
+        base = build(params, arch)
+        built_here = ln_prologue.build_ln_dual_gemm.cache_info().currsize > before
+        plan = base if built_here else ln_prologue.LnDualGemmPlan(params=base.params, module=base.module, launch=base.module.compile.__wrapped__())
+        return _SUBSTRATE_PLANS.setdefault(key, plan)
+
+
+def _compile_contraction(cudnn_module, channels: int, batch: int, n_res: int, direction: str, tile: str, device_index: int):
+    """The compiled FROST GEMM instance of the contraction for ``(c * B, direction, tile, dtype, device)`` -- M / N / K are symbolic in the
+    kernel, the batch count is baked, so the cache key is the folded batch, not N.  Keyed on the PLAN's device (not the current one): the
+    caller enters ``torch.cuda.device(device_index)`` around the compile, so a plan for ``cuda:1`` never binds a module loaded on ``cuda:0``."""
+    from cudnn.gemm.frost.compiler import jit_from_cudnn_graph
+    from cudnn.gemm.frost.tile_config import by_name
+
+    index = int(device_index)
+    key = (channels * batch, direction, tile, "bf16", index)
+    with _K2_LOCK:
+        hit = _K2_CACHE.get(key)
+        if hit is not None:
+            return hit
+    graph = k2.contraction_graph(cudnn_module, channels, n_res, direction, batch=batch, padded=True)
+    compiled = jit_from_cudnn_graph(graph, config=by_name(tile))
+    with _K2_LOCK:
+        return _K2_CACHE.setdefault(key, compiled)
+
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# The drop-in function (cuEquivariance's signature)
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+_PLAN_LOCK = threading.Lock()
+_PLANS: Dict[Tuple[Any, ...], TriangleMultiplicativeUpdateFwd] = {}
+_WEIGHTS: "OrderedDict[Tuple[Any, ...], Tuple[TriMulWeights, tuple]]" = OrderedDict()
+_WEIGHTS_MAX = 8
+
+_PRECISION_DEFAULT = ("NONE", "DEFAULT")
+_PRECISION_BF16 = ("BF16", "BFLOAT16")
+
+
+def _parse_precision(precision) -> str:
+    """cuEquivariance's ``precision`` spellings -> ``"default"`` (bf16 inputs required) or ``"bfloat16"`` (cast wider inputs); the
+    rest (``"mxfp8"``, ``"ieee"``, ``"tf32"``, ...) are typed declines."""
+    if precision is None:
+        return "default"
+    name = None
+    if isinstance(precision, str):
+        name = precision.upper()
+    elif isinstance(precision, int) and not isinstance(precision, bool):
+        name = {-1: "NONE", 0: "DEFAULT", 5: "BFLOAT16", 4: "MXFP8", 3: "IEEE", 1: "TF32", 2: "TF32X3"}.get(precision, str(precision))
+    elif hasattr(precision, "name"):
+        name = str(precision.name).upper()
+    else:
+        raise ValueError(f"precision must be None, a string or a cuEquivariance Precision, got {type(precision).__name__}")
+    if name in _PRECISION_DEFAULT:
+        return "default"
+    if name in _PRECISION_BF16:
+        return "bfloat16"
+    if name == "MXFP8":
+        raise NotImplementedError("precision='mxfp8' (block-scaled a / b operands) is not served by triangle_multiplicative_update yet")
+    raise NotImplementedError(f"precision={precision!r} is not served by triangle_multiplicative_update (bf16 arithmetic only: None / 'default' / 'bfloat16')")
+
+
+def _tensor_identity(t: Optional[torch.Tensor]):
+    """A parameter's identity for the weight cache: address, storage offset, shape, strides, dtype, device and torch's in-place version
+    counter.  An INFERENCE tensor (created under ``torch.inference_mode()``) has no version counter -- ``t._version`` raises -- so
+    :func:`_cached_weights` bypasses the cache for a set that holds one; this is reached for ordinary tensors only."""
+    if t is None:
+        return None
+    return (t.data_ptr(), t.storage_offset(), tuple(t.shape), tuple(t.stride()), t.dtype, str(t.device), t._version)
+
+
+def _has_inference_tensor(params: tuple) -> bool:
+    return any(t is not None and t.is_inference() for t in params)
+
+
+def _cached_weights(params: tuple, cast: bool) -> TriMulWeights:
+    """One prepared weight set per PARAMETER IDENTITY (address, shape, strides, dtype, device and torch's in-place version counter
+    of each of the twelve tensors); the entry keeps a reference to the source tensors so an address cannot be recycled under it.
+    A bounded LRU: a model switches parameter sets rarely, a training loop bumps the version counter and misses (one re-interleave).
+
+    A set holding an INFERENCE tensor (``t.is_inference()``: created under ``torch.inference_mode()``, which keeps no version counter)
+    has no identity an in-place update would change, so it is prepared on EVERY call and never cached -- the documented cost of
+    inference-mode parameters (a constant version in the key would serve stale weights after an in-place update made inside inference
+    mode).  Create the parameters outside inference mode, or prepare them once with :func:`prepare_weights` and the class API."""
+    if _has_inference_tensor(params):
+        return prepare_weights(*params, cast_to_bf16=cast)
+    key = (cast,) + tuple(_tensor_identity(t) for t in params)
+    with _PLAN_LOCK:
+        hit = _WEIGHTS.get(key)
+        if hit is not None:
+            _WEIGHTS.move_to_end(key)
+            return hit[0]
+    prepared = prepare_weights(*params, cast_to_bf16=cast)
+    with _PLAN_LOCK:
+        _WEIGHTS[key] = (prepared, tuple(t for t in params if t is not None))
+        _WEIGHTS.move_to_end(key)
+        while len(_WEIGHTS) > _WEIGHTS_MAX:
+            _WEIGHTS.popitem(last=False)
+    return prepared
+
+
+def _cached_plan(x: torch.Tensor, direction: str, c: int, has_mask: bool, has_in_bias: bool, has_out_bias: bool, eps: float) -> TriangleMultiplicativeUpdateFwd:
+    key = (tuple(x.shape), x.dtype, str(x.device), direction, int(c), bool(has_mask), bool(has_in_bias), bool(has_out_bias), float(eps))
+    with _PLAN_LOCK:
+        plan = _PLANS.get(key)
+    if plan is not None:
+        return plan
+    plan = TriangleMultiplicativeUpdateFwd(x, direction, c_hidden=c, has_mask=has_mask, has_in_bias=has_in_bias, has_out_bias=has_out_bias, eps=eps)
+    plan.check_support()
+    plan.compile()
+    with _PLAN_LOCK:
+        return _PLANS.setdefault(key, plan)
+
+
+def triangle_multiplicative_update(
+    x: torch.Tensor,
+    direction: str = "outgoing",
+    mask: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None,
+    norm_in_weight: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None,
+    norm_in_bias: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None,
+    p_in_weight: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None,
+    p_in_bias: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None,
+    g_in_weight: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None,
+    g_in_bias: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None,
+    norm_out_weight: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None,
+    norm_out_bias: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None,
+    p_out_weight: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None,
+    p_out_bias: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None,
+    g_out_weight: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None,
+    g_out_bias: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None,
+    eps: float = 1e-5,
+    precision=None,
+    *,
+    out: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None,
+    stream=None,
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """The triangle multiplicative update of ``x`` (``[B, N, N, c_z]`` or ``[N, N, c_z]`` bf16) -- cuEquivariance's signature
+    (``cuequivariance_ops_torch.triangle_multiplicative_update``, 0.12.0) with two keyword-only additions: ``out`` (write into this
+    bf16 tensor instead of allocating: ``[B, N, N, c_z]``, or ``[N, N, c_z]`` at ``B = 1``, contiguous, its bytes disjoint from ``x``, the
+    mask, every parameter and the workspace -- an intersecting byte range is a typed ``ValueError`` before any launch, since the output
+    stage reads ``x`` while it writes ``out``; a caller's ``out`` is returned AS GIVEN, whatever its rank) and ``stream`` (a raw CUDA
+    stream handle the allocations and launches are ordered on; None = torch's current stream).  Returns the update (the caller adds the
+    residual), shaped like ``x`` when the function allocated it.
+
+    Differences from cuEquivariance, all typed: the eight weights are REQUIRED (no implicit random initialisation); ``precision`` is
+    None / ``'default'`` (bf16 inputs required) or ``'bfloat16'`` (wider inputs cast once per call, as cuEquivariance does), ``'mxfp8'`` and
+    the IEEE / TF32 modes decline; a non-contiguous ``x`` declines; autograd is not registered yet, so under grad mode an input or
+    parameter with ``requires_grad`` is a typed decline (``NotImplementedError``), never a tensor without a ``grad_fn`` -- call under
+    ``torch.no_grad()`` or detach for inference.  A mask of any real or bool dtype is cast once per call to the kernels' bf16 ``[B, N, N]`` (no copy when
+    it already is).  One compiled plan per (shape, direction, flags) and one prepared weight set per parameter identity (address, shape,
+    strides, dtype, device, in-place version counter) are cached in the process; parameters created under ``torch.inference_mode()``
+    carry no version counter and are prepared on every call instead (create them outside inference mode, or prepare them once with
+    :func:`prepare_weights` and the class API); warm a shape before capturing a CUDA graph around this call.
+    """
+    from cudnn._torch_stream import stream_context
+
+    if direction not in DIRECTIONS:
+        raise ValueError(f"direction must be one of {DIRECTIONS}, got {direction!r}")
+    mode = _parse_precision(precision)
+    cast = mode == "bfloat16"
+    if not isinstance(x, torch.Tensor):
+        raise TypeError(f"x must be a torch.Tensor, got {type(x).__name__}")
+    squeeze = x.ndim == 3
+    x4 = x.unsqueeze(0) if squeeze else x
+    if x4.ndim != 4 or x4.shape[1] != x4.shape[2]:
+        raise ValueError(f"x must be [B, N, N, c_z] or [N, N, c_z], got {tuple(x.shape)}")
+    # `out` is validated BEFORE anything is done with it (a non-tensor used to fail at its unsqueeze, after the plan was built): tensor-ness and
+    # rank here, dtype / shape / contiguity / device / aliasing by execute's argument check; it is returned as given (squeezed never).
+    if out is not None:
+        if not isinstance(out, torch.Tensor):
+            raise TypeError(f"out must be a torch.Tensor (bf16, shaped like x) or None, got {type(out).__name__}")
+        if out.ndim not in (3, 4):
+            raise ValueError(f"out must be [B, N, N, c_z] (or [N, N, c_z] at B = 1) like x, got shape {tuple(out.shape)}")
+    if p_in_weight is None or p_in_weight.ndim != 2 or p_in_weight.shape[0] % 2:
+        raise ValueError("p_in_weight is required and must be [2 c, c_z] (rows [a; b])")
+    for name, w in (
+        ("norm_in_weight", norm_in_weight),
+        ("norm_in_bias", norm_in_bias),
+        ("g_in_weight", g_in_weight),
+        ("norm_out_weight", norm_out_weight),
+        ("norm_out_bias", norm_out_bias),
+        ("p_out_weight", p_out_weight),
+        ("g_out_weight", g_out_weight),
+    ):
+        if w is None:
+            raise ValueError(f"{name} is required (this API never initialises parameters implicitly)")
+    c = int(p_in_weight.shape[0]) // 2
+    _autograd_decline(
+        [
+            ("x", x),
+            ("mask", mask),
+            ("norm_in_weight", norm_in_weight),
+            ("norm_in_bias", norm_in_bias),
+            ("p_in_weight", p_in_weight),
+            ("p_in_bias", p_in_bias),
+            ("g_in_weight", g_in_weight),
+            ("g_in_bias", g_in_bias),
+            ("norm_out_weight", norm_out_weight),
+            ("norm_out_bias", norm_out_bias),
+            ("p_out_weight", p_out_weight),
+            ("p_out_bias", p_out_bias),
+            ("g_out_weight", g_out_weight),
+            ("g_out_bias", g_out_bias),
+            ("out", out),
+        ]
+    )
+    device = x4.device
+    with stream_context(stream, device):
+        if x4.dtype != torch.bfloat16:
+            if not cast:
+                raise NotImplementedError(

+"""The triangle multiplicative update's performance knobs and their MEASURED defaults -- the one place the API reads a tile or a tile order from.
+
+Every axis here is performance-only: a plan computes the same function (bitwise, the tests pin it) under any value of its domain, so a caller
+or an autotuner may pick freely.  Numerics modes (``affine_fold``, ``fuse_residual`` of the output stage) are NOT knobs: they change the
+function and stay op attributes the API never sets.
+
+  ``k2_tile``        the FROST GEMM tile config of the contraction (:data:`K2_TILE_DOMAIN`, catalog names): the 2-CTA 256 x 256 pair tile,
+                     the same with the A operand multicast across 2 / 4 CTAs, the 1-CTA 128 x 128 tile, the same with B multicast across 2.
+  ``k1_pass_order``  the projection stage's tile order (``"interleaved"``: both passes of a row block adjacent, the second ``x`` read an L2 hit;
+                     ``"major"``: every row block of pass 0 before pass 1).
+  ``k3_prologue``    the output stage's MN-major LayerNorm form (``"mn_major"`` in place; ``"transpose"`` into the K-major layout).
+  ``clc_stages``     the two LayerNorm-prologue stages' scheduler ring depth.
+  ``k_block``        the two LayerNorm-prologue stages' row tile: k's per 256-row pair tile (:data:`K_BLOCK_DOMAIN`; the substrate's rule
+                     ``default_k_block`` when a record leaves it unset -- 256 from N = 256, else the next power of two >= N).  At N = 384 the
+                     rule's 256 pads 25 % of every pair tile's rows; 128 pads none (the lever measured in the perf campaign).
+  ``ln_pass_form``   the two stages' LayerNorm pass form (:data:`LN_PASS_FORMS`: ``"registers"`` = the row held in registers between the passes;
+                     ``"smem"`` / ``"smem_rolled"`` = the row re-read from the SMEM stage in every pass, unrolled / rolled chunk loops -- the
+                     rolled form has no K = 256 spills; ``"smem_rolled_pf"`` = the rolled form with the next chunk's loads pipelined one
+                     iteration ahead; all bitwise the same output.  ``"smem_rolled_tree"`` = the pipelined form with four partial sums per
+                     statistics pass: a different fp32 summation order (:data:`LN_PASS_FORMS_REORDERED`), admitted as a caller's knob, never
+                     a pick of this table).
+  ``epi_math``       the two stages' gated-epilogue arithmetic form (:data:`EPI_MATHS`: ``"scalar"`` / ``"packed"`` fp32x2 pairs; bitwise).
+  ``min_blocks_per_mp``  the two stages' ``.minnctapersm`` launch hint (:data:`MIN_BLOCKS_PER_MP_DOMAIN`: 0 = the rendering as shipped, its
+                     register split dropped by ptxas; 1 = the hint under which ptxas honours the split -- bitwise the same output).  An OVERRIDE
+                     axis only: ``None`` (the table never sets it) means the per-RENDERING rule :func:`register_split_hint`, applied at compile
+                     time with each stage's bias flag, because the fact it answers -- does this rendering spill at the flat allocation? -- is a
+                     property of (kernel, width, bias arm, LayerNorm / epilogue form), not of N or B.
+  ``ln_once``        the two LayerNorm-prologue stages' work item (:data:`LN_ONCE_FORMS`: ``""`` = one GEMM tile, the row block's A rows re-streamed
+                     and re-normalised per (pass, N tile); ``"block"`` = the whole row block held resident in SMEM and LayerNormed ONCE across its
+                     passes x N tiles; ``"passes"`` = (row block, one N tile) across the passes -- the finer persistent tail for small N; bitwise the
+                     same output).  The output stage runs one pass, so it takes ``"block"`` at c = 256 only (two N tiles) and keeps today's item
+                     elsewhere (the substrate's typed decline of a one-tile item, resolved in the API's stage-parameter builder, stated); a geometry
+                     axis of the table (the persistent tail is a function of N and B), OFF in every pick until its A/B/A lands a per-bucket default.
+
+:func:`recommend` is the table -- the best MEASURED configuration per geometry on the 212-SM Rubin perf-node class, keyed by hidden width ``c``,
+N bucket, batch bucket and direction (and, appended, the device's compute capability ``cc``: the SM100 COLUMN below is its own MEASURED table --
+every axis swept on a 152-SM GB200 perf node (lock 1830 MHz) as a single-axis arm against the seeded pick, in-process control twins, graph replay
+>= 100 x 3, the fp64 oracle on every arm, for N >= 256 at B 1 / 4 in both directions; the N < 256 floors carry the Rubin picks with the recorded
+contraction tile until measured there, and the register-split hint rows are per column): a bucket table (width, N) carries the complete knob set, and a short refinement table overrides ONE axis
+where a cell of the measured grid (B in {1, 4}, both directions) beat the bucket's pick decisively in every pass that measured it.  A geometry
+nobody timed takes the nearest measured bucket's pick (N: the first floor at or below it; B: 4 from B >= 4, else 1), never a guess outside the
+domain.  :func:`resolve` merges a caller's ``k2_tile`` / ``knobs`` over it -- a :class:`TriMulKnobs` is a PARTIAL record: an axis left ``None``

+#            still spills half).
+#

+# words into the same additions in the same order, bitwise), measured STANDALONE on both LayerNorm-prologue kernels over the heuristics' complete pick
+# (graph replay, 100 x 3, control pair <= 0.4 %, every arm bitwise the pick, the 212-SM Rubin class at the 2376 lock; bias off AND on):
+#   c = 256: K1 +2.9 / +2.9 / +3.0 / +3.2 % (bias off) and +5.2 / +5.1 / +5.2 / +5.6 % (bias on) at N 512 x 1 / 384 x 1 / 256 x 4 / 1024 x 1, K3

+#            and +21.9 / +20.2 / +21.9 / +22.5 % (bias on, no spill in either: 278 -> 228 us) -- every cell of every measured bucket, the same sign in

+# adds +0.2..+3.5 % on top (K3 c 256 +25.0..+25.3 % vs the pick with the biases, +32.5..+36.0 % without; K1 c 256 +5.3..+6.1 %) and is NEVER a pick of

+#            LayerNorm it removes.  Every c = 256 pick: ln_once="block" (the "passes" item, LN 4 -> 2 per block, takes roughly half the gain: K1 +46..+80 %).
+#   c = 128: K1 only (the output stage's one-tile item is the substrate's typed decline there), on the buckets whose pick is the pass-MAJOR order:
+#            +43 / +44 / +53 / +53 % (bias off) and +45 / +45 / +49 / +53 % (bias on) at N 512 x 1 / 256 x 4 / 1024 x 4 / 768 x 1 (65 -> 45 us at 512 x 1
+#            off; 1000 x 3, CLEAN windows) -> ln_once="block" on the 512 / 768 / 1024 floors and on the (256, B >= 4) refinement (whose order is major);
+#            the buckets picking the INTERLEAVED order (256 x 1, 384) cannot take the lever as is (the pass must live inside the item: a typed decline);
+#            their candidate ln_once="block" + the major order, measured against the interleaved pick WITH the major order alone as the control: K1
+#            standalone +16.7 / +15.0 % at 256 x 1, +30.4 / +32.4 % at 384 x 1, +44.5 / +41.9 % at 384 x 4 (bias off / on) where the major order alone
+#            reads -0.3..-2.6 % (the lever carries it); the whole call +8.1 / +8.1 % at 256 x 128 x 1 and +12.5 / +13.4 % at 384 x 128 x 1 -> the 256
+#            and 384 floors take ("major", ln_once="block"); the 129 and 0 floors (N < 256: 0.6-1.2 tile-waves at B 1, the coarser item most exposed)
+#            stay as shipped until measured.
+def _pick(
+    k2_tile: str,
+    k1_pass_order: str,
+    k3_prologue: str,
+    clc_stages: int,
+    ln_pass_form: str,
+    epi_math: str,
+    ln_once: str = "",
+    ln_once_b_stages: Optional[int] = None,
+) -> TriMulKnobs:
+    """One COMPLETE bucket pick in axis order (the row tile ``k_block`` is left to :func:`default_k_block`; the LayerNorm-once item ``ln_once`` is OFF
+    unless a bucket's A/B/A set it; ``ln_once_b_stages`` (appended) = the item's B-ring depth where a bucket's A/B/A set it, else the shipped ring)."""
+    return TriMulKnobs(
+        k2_tile=k2_tile,
+        k1_pass_order=k1_pass_order,
+        k3_prologue=k3_prologue,
+        clc_stages=clc_stages,
+        ln_pass_form=ln_pass_form,
+        epi_math=epi_math,
+        ln_once=ln_once,

+# REPRODUCED when the refined table was measured as the base; the bucket keeps its pick where the other batch or direction lost.  Keys may repeat
+# across rows only for different axes (pinned by the tests).  Margins: +X % = t_bucket_pick / t_refined - 1 (the pass that found it; as the base).
+#   c = 128, N <= 128, B = 1, incoming:       ring depth 1   +1.87 % (as base +1.75 %; the outgoing twin -0.34 %, B = 4 -0.5..-0.6 %)

+#: The arch column a compute capability reads: Blackwell (10.0 / 10.3) the SM100 column, everything else -- Rubin, an unknown part, or ``None``
+#: (no device at hand: a CPU declaration, whose ``check_support`` declines before any launch) -- the Rubin table.  The heuristics never
+#: decline a part; the API's ``check_support`` does.
+_SM100_CCS = ((10, 0), (10, 3))

+
+def arch_column_for_cc(cc) -> str:
+    """``"sm100"`` for compute capability 10.0 / 10.3, ``"sm107"`` otherwise (including ``None``)."""
+    if cc is None:
+        return "sm107"
+    return "sm100" if tuple(int(x) for x in cc) in _SM100_CCS else "sm107"
+
+
+def _nearest_width(c: int) -> int:
+    widths = sorted(_PICKS)
+    return min(widths, key=lambda w: (abs(w - int(c)), w))
+
+
+def batch_bucket(batch: int) -> int:
+    """The measured batch bucket a batch size falls in: the largest member of :data:`BATCH_BUCKETS` at or below it (1 below 4)."""
+    b = int(batch)
+    return max((x for x in BATCH_BUCKETS if x <= b), default=BATCH_BUCKETS[0])
+
+
+def _bucket_floor(n_res: int, table: Tuple[Tuple[int, TriMulKnobs], ...]) -> Tuple[int, TriMulKnobs]:
+    for floor, knobs in table:
+        if n_res >= floor:
+            return floor, knobs
+    return table[-1]
+
+
+def k2_tile_for(n_res: int, channels: int = 128, batch: int = 1, direction: str = "outgoing", cc=None) -> str:
+    """The contraction's tile config for ``(N, c, B, direction)`` from the measured table (``cc`` appended: the SM100 column on 10.0 / 10.3)."""
+    return recommend(n_res, channels, batch, direction, cc=cc).k2_tile
+
+
+def default_k_block(n_res: int) -> int:
+    """The row tile a bare declaration runs at ``n_res``: the substrate's rule (``cudnn.gemm.frost.ln_prologue.default_k_block``: 256 from N = 256,
+    else the next power of two >= N) held inside :data:`K_BLOCK_DOMAIN` (below N = 33 the API declines before any launch; the clamp keeps the record in
+    the vocabulary there) -- EXCEPT where the 128-row block computes fewer rows than the 256 one (``N mod 256`` in 1..128 from N = 256: at N = 384 the
+    rule's 256 pads 25 % of every pair tile, 128 pads none), measured on the 212-SM Rubin perf-node class as the faster tile there (the lever's record:
+    N = 384, c = 128 and 256, B = 1 and 4, both directions; the per-CTA TMA box is the same as 256's, only the scheduler walks fewer tiles)."""
+    n = int(n_res)
+    kb = max(_substrate_default_k_block(n), K_BLOCK_DOMAIN[0])
+    if n >= PAIR_TILE_ROWS and -(-n // 128) * 128 < -(-n // PAIR_TILE_ROWS) * PAIR_TILE_ROWS:
+        kb = 128
+    return kb

+# THE RENDERING RULE -- the `.minnctapersm` launch hint per (stage, width, bias arm, LayerNorm form, epilogue form).  Not a geometry axis: the fact it
+# answers is whether THIS rendering spills at the flat register allocation ptxas picks when the body's setmaxnreg split is dropped (no `.maxnreg`,
+# no `.minnctapersm`: C7508).  The host SASS of every production rendering (sm_107a trace-compile, nvdisasm) says where: every bias-OFF rendering
+# is allocated EXACTLY 80 registers (= 65536 / (2 x 384 threads): ptxas's two-CTAs-per-SM target, reached with a few spills when the body's demand
+# sits near it) while every bias-ON one is allocated its demand (97-114) -- and the one rendering whose spills reach the hot path is the output
+# stage at c = 256 with the rolled LayerNorm form and no output biases: REG 80 / STACK 24, 5 STL / 7 LDL = three swizzled staging-store addresses
+# and two row-decode constants reloaded per tile ahead of the epilogue's TMEM loads (69.8 k local requests in ncu), +7.0..+8.0 % on the kernel
+# against its bias-ON twin on all nine c = 256 cells of the matrix, +3.0..+4.0 % on the whole call.  The hint lifts C7508 (the split honoured:
+# USETMAXREG 6, the epilogue + LayerNorm warps at 232, the producers at 24; the cubin byte-identical to a `.maxnreg 168` build); a row enters this
+# table only with its A/B/A on the 212-SM Rubin perf-node class (the same protocol as the geometry table), and the default 0 keeps every other
+# production rendering's cubin byte-identical to the one measured before the axis existed.
+# Keyed (stage, width, has_bias, ln_pass_form, epi_math, pass_order, ln_once) -- the projection stage's tile ORDER is part of the rendering (the
+# `interleaved` K1 renderings carry 4 STL / 13 LDL of role-prologue values UNDER the hint where the `major` ones carry none); the output stage has no
+# order (None); the LayerNorm WORK ITEM (`ln_once`) is part of it too (below: every row names the per-tile item).
+# MEASURED ROWS (the A/B/A of the rule as it lands; the bias-OFF rows first, then the bias-ON rows of the c 128 register-form renderings that run
+# the bias-path epilogue fold -- a bias-ON rendering is allocated its demand (no spill either way), and the honoured split still pays there):
+# the projection stage at c 128 with the pass-MAJOR tile order (the heuristics' pick from N = 512 and at 256 B 4): whole-call A/B/A on one exclusive GPU of the 212-SM Rubin perf-node class (lock 2376), in-process arm + control twins, 100-400 x 3 graph replay, two passes with the same sign -- the register form +1.6 / +1.5 / +1.7 / +1.8 % at 512:128:1 / 256:128:4 / 768:128:1 / 768:128:4 (its 1 / 1 STACK-8 spill gone; K1 itself +3.8 %), the rolled form +1.1..+1.2 % at 1024:128:1 / 512:128:4 / 1024:128:4 (REG 80 flat -> the 232 / 24 split, no spill either way; K1 +2.5 %);
+# NOT a row: the INTERLEAVED rolled projection renderings (N 256 B 1, 384) -0.1..-0.7 % (4 / 13 role-prologue spills under the hint), the output stage at c 256 bias off -0.1 / -0.1 / +0.0 % (its 5 / 7 epilogue spills vanish, the kernel time does not move: 298 vs 297 us -- the bias-off deficit against the bias-on body is elsewhere), the bias-ON renderings NOT named below (the identity controls +0.0 %; the rolled-form K1 bias-on cells +0.33 / +0.35 % under the hint = inside the bar).
+# the hint rows (whole call, bias ON, the same node class): the K1-only row +2.57 / +2.39 / +2.52 / +2.52 % at 512:128:1 / 768:128:1 / 256:128:4 / 768:128:4 (the CUPTI split: K1 71.8 -> 68.1 us = -5.2 %, K3 unchanged), +0.23 / +0.26 % on the rolled-form K1 cells 1024:128:1 / 512:128:4 (inside the bar), -1.15 % on the interleaved 384:128:4 (role-prologue spills under the split, as at bias off); the K3-only row -0.10..+0.11 % on every cell (neutral: not a row); both stages hinted together +2.37..+2.61 % = the K1 row's gain
+# THE WORK ITEM IS PART OF THE KEY (the LayerNorm-once item `ln_once`, measured 2026-10-13 on the landed picks, the same node class and protocol):
+# under `ln_once="block"` the item's +4 live words in the 24-register producer roles turn the honoured split into spills the per-tile item never
+# had (host SASS, sm_107a: the c 128 register form 0 / 0 -> 4 STL / 13 LDL at STACK 16, the rolled form 1 / 1 -> 9 / 15 at STACK 24, the c 256
+# pf forms 2 / 2 -> 9 / 16 (K1) and 5 / 6 -> 25 / 26 at STACK 144 (K3)), and the whole call does not pay for them: the rule's hint vs
+# `min_blocks_per_mp=0` over the landed picks (one process per knob set, in-process control twins, graph replay, the fp64 oracle on every cell;
+# the three cells unhinted under both as the identity control: +0.01 / -0.31 / +0.11 %) -- the UNHINTED call is faster by 1.10 / 1.28 / 0.69 /
+# 1.15 / 0.46 % at 512:128:1 / 768:128:1 / 1024:128:4 / 256:128:4 / 384:128:1 bias off (the register AND the rolled form) and within the noise at
+# 512:128:1 / 768:128:1 / 256:128:4 bias on (-0.15 / +0.17 / -0.15 %); standalone the rolled K1 loses 2.5 / 3.2 % hinted at 1024:4 / 256:1 and the
+# c 256 forms lose 6.1-7.0 % (K1) and 12.0 % (K3) (the standalone register-form K1 reads +0.7..+1.1 % hinted -- a `want_stats=True` rendering the
+# API never builds; the whole call is the landing evidence, as for every row above).  So every row names the PER-TILE item (`ln_once=""`): a bare
+# declaration whose pick carries the item (every c 128 bucket from N = 256, every c 256 bucket) runs UNHINTED -- the renderings the pins measured
+# at 0 / 0 (register) and 1 / 1 (rolled); a caller's `TriMulKnobs(ln_once="")` keeps the measured hint; "passes" has no row (unmeasured -> as shipped).
+_REGISTER_SPLIT_HINTS: Dict[Tuple[str, int, bool, str, str, Optional[str], str], int] = {
+    ("k1", 128, False, "registers", "packed", "major", ""): 1,
+    ("k1", 128, False, "smem_rolled", "packed", "major", ""): 1,
+    # under the block item this rendering runs unhinted (above); there the fold still beats `packed` +0.73 / +0.93 % on 768:128:1 / 768:128:4 and ties on
+    # 512:128:1 outgoing / incoming / 256:128:4 (+0.14 / +0.43 / -0.17 %; both arms unhinted, 212-SM Rubin class) -- the pick stands; `packed` + a
+    # block-keyed hint 1 read +0.68 / +0.79 / +0.51 % on 512:128:1 outgoing / incoming / 768:128:1 over it (two passes, not yet reproduced as the base)
+    ("k1", 128, True, "registers", "packed_biasfold", "major", ""): 1,
+}
+
+# THE SM100 COLUMN'S REGISTER-SPLIT ROW (compute capability 10.0 / 10.3) -- MEASURED 2026-10-14 on the same 152-SM GB200 perf node (lock 1830 MHz,
+# sampled; one exclusive GPU; the measured column as the base, the hinted twin and the seeded pick as in-process arms beside the pick, its control
+# twin, cuEq and torch; graph replay >= 100 x 3; every arm bitwise the pick and inside the API oracle): with BOTH stages under `.minnctapersm 1`
+# the c 128 REGISTER-form picks (the plain packed epilogue, the pass-major order, the block item, the biases on) run +1.56 / +1.22 % at 512 x 1,
+# +1.31 / +1.22 % at 768 x 1, +0.92 / +0.95 % at 1024 x 1, +0.87 / +0.80 % at 1536 x 1, +0.72 / +0.76 % at 2048 x 1, +1.13 / +1.23 % at 256 x 4,

+# rolled picks of the 384 bucket and the 256 bucket's incoming cell LOSE -2.98 / -3.25 % and -2.94 % hinted -- so the row names the register-form
+# K1 rendering only, and the output stage (the same transpose register rendering on every c 128 plan) stays unhinted until an arm separates its
+# share.  The sm_100a renderings under the hint: 0 / 0 spills, USETMAXREG 6, both stages; unlike Rubin, where the block item's hinted renderings
+# spill and the whole call runs faster unhinted, so the two columns' rows differ by design.
+_REGISTER_SPLIT_HINTS_SM100: Dict[Tuple[str, int, bool, str, str, Optional[str], str], int] = {
+    ("k1", 128, True, "registers", "packed", "major", "block"): 1,
+}
+
+
+def register_split_hint(
+    stage: str, channels: int, has_bias: bool, ln_pass_form: str, epi_math: str, pass_order: Optional[str] = None, ln_once: str = "", cc=None
+) -> int:
+    """The ``.minnctapersm`` hint a bare declaration hands the ``stage`` (``"k1"`` = the projection, ``"k3"`` = the output stage) rendering at this
+    hidden width, bias arm, LayerNorm / epilogue form, (K1) tile order and LayerNorm work item (``ln_once``; the stage's OWN item -- the output stage's
+    is ``""`` where the substrate declines a one-tile item): the MEASURED rows of :data:`_REGISTER_SPLIT_HINTS`, else 0 (the rendering as shipped;
+    every row names the per-tile item -- under the LayerNorm-once item the honoured split spills and the whole call runs faster unhinted).  A
+    caller's ``TriMulKnobs(min_blocks_per_mp=...)`` overrides it for both stages.  ``cc`` (appended) selects the column: the Rubin rows for 10.7 /
+    ``None``, :data:`_REGISTER_SPLIT_HINTS_SM100` (the rows measured on a GB200 for the SM100 column's own register-form renderings) for 10.0 / 10.3."""
+    if stage not in ("k1", "k3"):
+        raise ValueError(f"stage must be 'k1' or 'k3', got {stage!r}")
+    table = _REGISTER_SPLIT_HINTS if arch_column_for_cc(cc) == "sm107" else _REGISTER_SPLIT_HINTS_SM100
+    order = (str(pass_order) if pass_order is not None else None) if stage == "k1" else None
+    # the rows are keyed by RENDERING: the three packed epilogue forms differ only under `has_bias` and render ONE cubin without biases, so a
+    # bias-off lookup reads the family's row (`EPI_MATHS_PACKED`); a bias-on rendering is hinted only by a row naming its EXACT form
+    epm = "packed" if (not has_bias and str(epi_math) in EPI_MATHS_PACKED) else str(epi_math)
+    return table.get((stage, _nearest_width(channels), bool(has_bias), str(ln_pass_form), epm, order, str(ln_once or "")), 0)
+
+
+def recommend(n_res: int, channels: int = 128, batch: int = 1, direction: str = "outgoing", cc=None) -> TriMulKnobs:
+    """The measured default knob set for this geometry: the (width, N bucket) pick with the (batch bucket, direction) refinements applied, the
+    row tile from :func:`default_k_block` unless a pick or refinement sets it -- complete (every axis set).  ``cc`` (appended) selects the arch
+    column (:func:`arch_column_for_cc`: the SM100 column on compute capability 10.0 / 10.3, the Rubin table otherwise and for ``None``)."""
+    if direction not in k2.DIRECTIONS:
+        raise ValueError(f"direction must be one of {k2.DIRECTIONS}, got {direction!r}")
+    n_res = int(n_res)
+    width = _nearest_width(channels)
+    column = arch_column_for_cc(cc)
+    floor, knobs = _bucket_floor(n_res, _PICKS_BY_ARCH[column][width])
+    bb = batch_bucket(batch)
+    for r_floor, r_batch, r_direction, override in _REFINEMENTS_BY_ARCH[column].get(width, ()):
+        if r_floor == floor and r_batch == bb and (r_direction is None or r_direction == direction):
+            knobs = override.merged_over(knobs)
+    if knobs.k_block is None:
+        knobs = replace(knobs, k_block=default_k_block(n_res))
+    return knobs
+
+
+def resolve(
+    n_res: int, channels: int, batch: int, direction: str, *, k2_tile: Optional[str] = None, knobs: Optional[TriMulKnobs] = None, cc=None
+) -> TriMulKnobs:
+    """The knob set a plan runs: :func:`recommend` for the geometry (and the device's ``cc``, appended), then the caller's ``knobs`` (its SET axes)
+    and ``k2_tile`` (one axis) over it -- always a complete record.  No validation here: ``check_support`` runs :func:`validate_knobs` so an
+    out-of-vocabulary name is a typed decline at the usual place (a ``knobs`` of the wrong type raises there too)."""
+    out = recommend(n_res, channels, batch, direction, cc=cc)
+    if knobs is not None and isinstance(knobs, TriMulKnobs):
+        out = knobs.merged_over(out)
+    elif knobs is not None:
+        return knobs  # not a TriMulKnobs: handed through for validate_knobs to raise the TypeError
+    if k2_tile is not None:
+        out = replace(out, k2_tile=str(k2_tile))
+    return out
+
