+
+    def _io_dtype(self, cudnn):
+        return cudnn.data_type.HALF if self.dtype == torch.float16 else cudnn.data_type.BFLOAT16
+
+    def _stats_layout(self) -> Tuple[Tuple[int, int, int, int], Tuple[int, int, int, int]]:
+        n, h, s = self.n, self.h, self.s_q
+        return (n, h, s, 1), (h * s, s, 1, 1)
+
+    def _build_graph(self):
+        """The ``sdpa`` graph of ONE outer batch entry on the declared layouts, planned; returns ``(graph, index of the row's plan)`` or
+        raises the engine row's own reason."""
+        import cudnn
+
+        io = self._io_dtype(cudnn)
+        f32 = cudnn.data_type.FLOAT
+        g = cudnn.pygraph(io_data_type=io, intermediate_data_type=f32, compute_data_type=f32)
+        tq = g.tensor(dim=list(self.q4[0]), stride=list(self.q4[1]), data_type=io, name="q")
+        tk = g.tensor(dim=list(self.k4[0]), stride=list(self.k4[1]), data_type=io, name="k")
+        tv = g.tensor(dim=list(self.v4[0]), stride=list(self.v4[1]), data_type=io, name="v")
+        tb = g.tensor(dim=list(self.bias4[0]), stride=list(self.bias4[1]), data_type=io, name="bias")
+        kw: Dict[str, Any] = dict(name="sdpa", q=tq, k=tk, v=tv, bias=tb, generate_stats=self.want_lse, attn_scale=self.scale)
+        order = [tq, tk, tv, tb]
+        if self.mask_form == "mask":
+            tm = g.tensor(dim=[self.n, 1, 1, self.s_kv], stride=[self.s_kv, self.s_kv, self.s_kv, 1], data_type=cudnn.data_type.BOOLEAN, name="kv_mask")

+            order.append(tm)

+            # seq_len_q/seq_len_kv"), and the kernel bounds the live Q rows by seq_len_q.  Every Q row is live here, so seq_len_q is the
+            # constant S_q on every entry: `execute` writes it into the caller's workspace on the launch stream and binds that region
+            # (execute scratch carved from the workspace, declared by get_workspace_size -- never a plan-owned tensor, which would be
+            # released at GC time, possibly inside someone else's CUDA-graph capture).  Nothing is allocated at build or at execute.
+            slk = g.tensor(dim=[self.n, 1, 1, 1], stride=[1, 1, 1, 1], data_type=cudnn.data_type.INT32, name="seq_len_kv")

+        try:
+            o, stats = g.sdpa(**kw)

+            if self.want_lse:

+                stats.set_output(True).set_dim(list(dim)).set_stride(list(stride)).set_data_type(f32)

+        names = [g.get_plan_name_at_index(i) for i in range(len(g.plans))]
+        ours = [i for i, nm in enumerate(names) if nm == ENGINE_ROW or nm.startswith(ENGINE_ROW + "[")]
+        idx = next((i for i in ours if getattr(g.plans[i].knobs, "split_kv", None) in (None, 1)), None)
+        if idx is None:
+            raise NotImplementedError(f"triangle_attention: the FROST row {ENGINE_ROW} declines this declaration -- {self._engine_reason(g, None)}")

+        self.plan_name = names[idx]

+
+    @staticmethod
+    def _engine_reason(g, error) -> str:
+        """The engine row's own typed decline string for this graph (``engines.analyze_for`` -> ``mismatch``), the FE's error as the fallback."""
+        try:
+            from cudnn.sdpa.fwd import engines
+
+            spec = next(sp for sp in engines.ENGINE_SPECS if sp.name == ENGINE_ROW)
+            _facts, why = engines.analyze_for(spec, g, None)
+            if why:
+                return f"{ENGINE_ROW}: {why}"
+        except Exception as probe_error:  # noqa: BLE001 -- the probe must never hide the decline itself
+            return f"{ENGINE_ROW} could not be asked ({type(probe_error).__name__}: {probe_error})" + (f"; {error}" if error is not None else "")
+        return f"{ENGINE_ROW} proposed no unsplit plan" + (f"; {error}" if error is not None else "")
+
+    # -- compile ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+    def compile(self) -> None:
+        """Pin the FROST row's plan on the graph and build it on the declaration's device (a compiled launchable is bound to the CUDA
+        context it was loaded in); records the plan's name, its public knob record and its workspace requirement."""
+        self._ensure_support_checked()
+        import cudnn
+
+        g = self._graph
+        with torch.cuda.device(self.device_index):
+            g.select_plan(self._plan_index)
+            g.check_support()
+            g.build_plans()
+            self._plan_workspace_bytes = int(g.get_workspace_size())

+        self._workspace_bytes = workspace_bytes(self._plan_workspace_bytes, self._n_q_lens, self._n_kv_lens, self._n_mask_stage)

+            # The derivation kernel's artifact for this device, built HERE so the first execute (a graph capture included) compiles nothing.
+            from .kernels.prefix_lengths import prefix_lengths_plan
+
+            prefix_lengths_plan(self.device_index)
+        _engine_id, record = g.get_engine_and_knobs_at_index(self._plan_index)
+        self.knobs = dict(record) if record else {}
+        self._uids = tuple(t.uid for t in self._order)
+        self._frame = None  # the bound argument frame (built by the engine's binder on the first execute, pointers refreshed per call)
+        compiled = g._compiled_plans.get(self._plan_index)
+        self._compiled_plan = compiled
+        spec = getattr(getattr(compiled, "_prepared", None), "spec", None)
+        # The pointer-refresh path serves the plain dense launch only: a prepared launch without a split / combine, a quantized
+        # recipe, a native (C) binder or a ragged leg, and no workspace.  Anything else runs through the graph's execute.
+        self._fast_spec = (
+            spec
+            if (
+                spec is not None
+                and self._plan_workspace_bytes == 0
+                and getattr(spec, "combine", None) is None
+                and getattr(spec, "quant", None) is None
+                and getattr(spec, "native", None) is None

+            )
+            else None
+        )
+        self._compiled_kernel = g
+
+    def get_workspace_size(self) -> int:
+        """Bytes of the workspace ``execute`` needs: the plan's own requirement (0 on most declarations; the dense-mask form at an
+        ``S_kv`` that is not a multiple of the kv tile carries the engine's synthesized padding lengths) plus, on the ``kv_lengths`` and
+        ``prefix_mask`` forms, ``N`` int32 words for the Q-side lengths the graph's padding contract requires -- ``execute`` writes ``S_q``
+        there on its stream before the launches -- and, on the ``prefix_mask`` form, ``B * N`` int32 words for the KV lengths the device
+        derives (the fused kernel stages nothing).  Sized and carved by the SDPA adapters' shared recipe (:func:`workspace_bytes`,

+    # -- execute ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+    def _check_tensor(self, t, name: str, shape, stride, dtype, align: int = _TMA_ALIGN) -> None:
+        """One operand against the declaration; ``align`` is the base alignment ITS reader needs -- the binder's own rule per role
+        (16 bytes for the TMA-read q / k / v / bias / o, 4 for the int32 lengths and the fp32 lse, none for the byte mask), never a

+            raise ValueError(
+                f"{name} lives on {t.device}; this plan was declared on cuda:{self.device_index} and its kernel is loaded there (declare and compile one plan per device)"
+            )
+        if t.dtype != dtype:
+            raise ValueError(f"{name} must be {dtype} (the declaration), got {t.dtype}")

+    def _check_execute_args(self, q, k, v, bias, kv_lengths, o, lse, score_max, workspace, mask) -> None:

+        shape5 = (b, n, h, s_q, self.d)

+        self._check_tensor(k, "k", (b, n, self.h_kv, s_kv, self.d), (self.outer_strides[1],) + self.k4[1], self.dtype)

+            raise ValueError("o is required: the prepared API never allocates (the drop-in function does)")

+        elif self.mask_form in ("mask", "prefix_mask"):

+            if workspace.device.type != "cuda" or workspace.device.index != self.device_index:

+            if not workspace.is_contiguous():

+                    f"workspace must be contiguous (its chunks are carved as views of the caller's bytes), got strides {tuple(workspace.stride())}"

+    def execute(
+        self,
+        q: torch.Tensor,
+        k: torch.Tensor,
+        v: torch.Tensor,
+        bias: torch.Tensor,
+        kv_lengths: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None,
+        o: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None,
+        lse: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None,
+        score_max: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None,
+        workspace: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None,
+        current_stream=None,
+        *,
+        mask: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None,
+        check_prefix_mask: Optional[bool] = None,
+    ) -> None:
+        """Launch the plan on ``current_stream`` (None = torch's current stream on the plan's device): one launch per outer batch
+        entry.  Validates every tensor against the declaration, never converts or allocates.
+
+        Host path: the engine's prepared launch binds its argument frame ONCE per plan (the engine's own binder, on the first call --
+        every dtype / layout / alignment / span rule of the row); every later call re-checks the tensors against the declaration here
+        and refreshes the frame's POINTER slots (the geometry is the declaration's, fixed), then issues the kernel -- the host floor of
+        an eager call is the API's checks plus the launch itself.  A plan the fast path does not serve (a plan workspace, a split, a
+        native binder) runs through the graph's execute with the same operands.  The ``kv_lengths`` form first writes the Q-side lengths
+        (``S_q`` on every entry) into the caller's workspace on the same stream -- one driver memset, stream-ordered before the launches,
+        a memset node in a captured graph.  The ``prefix_mask`` form then derives the KV lengths from the boolean ``mask`` on the same
+        stream (:func:`_row_counts_on_device`: ONE launch of the row-popcount kernel into the lengths chunk -- no cast pass, no staging,

+        ``check_prefix_mask`` (that form only): True runs :func:`assert_prefix_mask` after the derivation -- the device-wide prefix test

+        if self._compiled_kernel is None:
+            raise RuntimeError("compile() must run before execute()")
+        self._check_execute_args(q, k, v, bias, kv_lengths, o, lse, score_max, workspace, mask)
+        stream_int = _stream_int(current_stream, self.device)
+        plan_ws = q_lens = kv_lens = stage = None
+        if self._workspace_bytes:
+            plan_ws, q_lens, kv_lens, stage = carve_workspace_chunks(
+                workspace, self._plan_workspace_bytes, self._n_q_lens, self._n_kv_lens, self._n_mask_stage, type(self).__name__
+            )
+        if q_lens is not None:
+            self._write_q_lengths(q_lens, stream_int)

+        else:
+            self._execute_graph(q, k, v, bias, kv_lengths, mask, o, lse, plan_ws, q_lens, stream_int)
+
+    def _write_q_lengths(self, q_lens: torch.Tensor, stream_int: int) -> None:
+        """The ``kv_lengths`` form: fill the carved ``N`` int32 Q-side lengths with ``S_q`` on the execute stream (one driver memset; no
+        allocation, no host synchronisation) -- the graph's padding contract requires a Q-side length tensor and the kernel bounds the
+        live Q rows by it; every Q row of a triangle-attention call is live."""
+        from cudnn._device import ensure_current_context
+        from cudnn.frost.buffers import fill_word_async
+
+        ensure_current_context(stream_int, self.device_index)
+        fill_word_async(q_lens.data_ptr(), self.n, self.s_q, stream_int)
+
+    def _derive_kv_lengths(self, mask: torch.Tensor, kv_lens: torch.Tensor, stream_int: int, check: Optional[bool]) -> torch.Tensor:
+        """The ``prefix_mask`` form: each row's True count, computed on the execute stream into the carved ``kv_lens`` chunk by ONE launch
+        of the row-popcount kernel (the artifact :meth:`compile` built for this device), returned as the ``(B, N, 1, 1, 1)`` int32 view
+        the ``kv_lengths`` form binds.  The mask is never read on the host; the optional debug check is."""
+        _row_counts_on_device(mask, kv_lens, stream_int)
+        lengths = kv_lens.view(self.batch, self.n, 1, 1, 1)
+        if check if check is not None else prefix_check_enabled():
+            assert_prefix_mask(mask, lengths)
+        return lengths
+
+    def _entry_views(self, q, k, v, bias, kv_lengths, mask, o, lse, b: int, q_lens=None) -> list:
+        """The per-entry buffers in the graph's operand order (the declaration's 4-D geometry); with ``q_lens`` (the carved Q-side
+        lengths) the ``kv_lengths`` form's ``(N, 1, 1, 1)`` view follows the KV lengths (the graph path), without it the role is bound
+        from the carved view's facts (the frame path)."""
+        bufs = [q[b], k[b], v[b], bias[0] if self.bias_broadcast_batch else bias[b]]

+        elif self.mask_form in ("kv_lengths", "prefix_mask"):

+            bufs.append(lse[b])
+        return bufs
+
+    def _execute_graph(self, q, k, v, bias, kv_lengths, mask, o, lse, plan_ws, q_lens, stream_int: int) -> None:

+        cudnn.set_stream(self._handle, stream_int)
+        g, handle, uids = self._compiled_kernel, self._handle, self._uids
+        for b in range(self.batch):
+            g.execute(tuple(self._entry_views(q, k, v, bias, kv_lengths, mask, o, lse, b, q_lens)), plan_ws, handle, tensor_uids=uids)
+
+    # The engine's frame slots the per-call pointers land in, by role: (slot name, element bytes of the buffer).
+    _PTR_SLOTS = (
+        ("q", "q_ptr", 2),
+        ("k", "k_ptr", 2),
+        ("v", "v_ptr", 2),
+        ("o", "o_ptr", 2),
+        ("bias", "bias_ptr", 2),
+        ("kv_mask", "kv_mask_ptr", 1),
+        ("seq_kv_lens", "meta_ptr", 4),
+        ("seq_q_lens", "seq_q_lens_addr", 4),
+        ("lse", "lse_ptr", 4),
+    )
+
+    def _bind_frame(self, q, k, v, bias, kv_lengths, mask, o, lse, q_lens, cu_stream, stream_int: int) -> None:
+        """The first call: the engine's binder validates entry 0's operands and builds the argument frame; the pointer slots and
+        each role's per-entry byte step are recorded for every later call.  The ``kv_lengths`` form's Q-side lengths role is the
+        carved workspace chunk (``q_lens``: ``N`` contiguous int32 words, its facts read like any operand's), shared by every entry."""
+        from cudnn.sdpa.fwd import prepared as prep
+
+        bufs = self._entry_views(q, k, v, bias, kv_lengths, mask, o, lse, 0)
+        roles = ["q", "k", "v", "bias"]
+        if self.mask_form == "mask":

+        elif self.mask_form in ("kv_lengths", "prefix_mask"):

+        steps = {
+            "q": self.outer_strides[0] * 2,
+            "k": self.outer_strides[1] * 2,
+            "v": self.outer_strides[2] * 2,
+            "o": self.o_outer_stride * 2,
+            "bias": 0 if self.bias_broadcast_batch else self.outer_strides[3] * 2,
+            "seq_q_lens": 0,  # one region, every entry's Q rows are live

+        for role, slot, _elem in self._PTR_SLOTS:

+        self._frame_slots = tuple(slots)

+    def _execute_frames(self, q, k, v, bias, kv_lengths, mask, o, lse, q_lens, stream_int: int) -> None:
+        from cudnn._device import ensure_current_context
+
+        ensure_current_context(stream_int, self.device_index)
+        cu_stream = self._compiled_plan._stream_handle(stream_int)
+        if self._frame is None:
+            self._bind_frame(q, k, v, bias, kv_lengths, mask, o, lse, q_lens, cu_stream, stream_int)
+        base = {"q": q.data_ptr(), "k": k.data_ptr(), "v": v.data_ptr(), "o": o.data_ptr(), "bias": bias.data_ptr()}
+        if mask is not None:
+            base["kv_mask"] = mask.data_ptr()
+        if kv_lengths is not None:
+            base["seq_kv_lens"] = kv_lengths.data_ptr()
+            base["seq_q_lens"] = q_lens.data_ptr()
+        if lse is not None:
+            base["lse"] = lse.data_ptr()
+        steps = {
+            "kv_mask": mask.stride(0) if mask is not None else 0,
+            "seq_kv_lens": kv_lengths.stride(0) * 4 if kv_lengths is not None else 0,
+            "lse": self.n * self.h * self.s_q * 4,
+        }
+        fn = self._fast_spec.fn
+        template = self._frame
+        template[self._frame_stream_slot] = cu_stream
+        for b in range(self.batch):
+            frame = list(template)
+            for role, slot, step in self._frame_slots:
+                frame[slot] = base[role] + b * (step if step is not None else steps[role])

+    def make_cuda_graph(self, q, k, v, bias, kv_lengths=None, o=None, lse=None, workspace=None, *, mask=None, warmup: int = 2) -> "torch.cuda.CUDAGraph":

+        contents may change between replays, their addresses may not).  ``warmup`` eager calls run first on a side stream.  The
+        ``kv_lengths`` form's workspace fill is captured with the launches (a memset node), so the workspace is required here as in
+        ``execute``; the ``prefix_mask`` form's derivation kernel is captured too (a replay follows the mask's contents).  The
+        warm-up calls run the prefix-mask debug check as the environment decides; the captured call never does (a synchronisation
+        inside a capture is an error)."""
+        side = torch.cuda.Stream(device=q.device)
+        side.wait_stream(torch.cuda.current_stream(q.device))
+        with torch.cuda.stream(side):
+            for _ in range(int(warmup)):
+                self.execute(q, k, v, bias, kv_lengths, o, lse, None, workspace, side.cuda_stream, mask=mask)
+        torch.cuda.current_stream(q.device).wait_stream(side)
+        torch.cuda.synchronize(q.device)
+        graph = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
+        with torch.cuda.graph(graph, stream=side):
+            self.execute(q, k, v, bias, kv_lengths, o, lse, None, workspace, side.cuda_stream, mask=mask, check_prefix_mask=False)
+        return graph

+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# The drop-in function (cuEquivariance's signature)
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+_PLAN_LOCK = threading.Lock()
+_PLANS: Dict[Tuple[Any, ...], TriangleAttentionFwd] = {}
+_COUNTS: Dict[str, int] = {}
+_WARNED: set = set()
+
+
+def copy_counters() -> Dict[str, int]:
+    """Snapshot of the function's COUNTED layout fallbacks since the last reset: ``fallback_copies`` (every copy) and per kind --
+    ``q_repack`` / ``k_repack`` / ``v_repack`` (an activation not in the kernel's token-major form), ``o_repack`` (the output copied
+    back into the caller's layout), ``bias_repack`` (a bias whose key dim is not contiguous or whose row stride is not a 16-byte
+    multiple: padded to ``S_kv`` rounded up to 8), ``bias_cast`` (an fp32 bias cast to the activations' dtype), ``mask_repack`` /
+    ``kv_lengths_repack`` (a non-contiguous mask / lengths tensor), ``out_copy`` (an ``out=`` tensor the kernel could not write
+    directly).  A model on its native layout should read 0 everywhere."""
+    with _PLAN_LOCK:
+        return dict(_COUNTS)
+
+
+def reset_copy_counters() -> None:
+    with _PLAN_LOCK:
+        _COUNTS.clear()
+
+
+def _count(kind: str, plan: Optional[TriangleAttentionFwd], what: str) -> None:
+    with _PLAN_LOCK:
+        _COUNTS[kind] = _COUNTS.get(kind, 0) + 1
+        _COUNTS["fallback_copies"] = _COUNTS.get("fallback_copies", 0) + 1
+        first = (kind, what) not in _WARNED
+        _WARNED.add((kind, what))
+    if plan is not None:
+        plan.fallback_copies += 1
+    if first:
+        warnings.warn(
+            f"cudnn.triangle_attention: {kind} -- {what}; the tensor is copied into the kernel's layout on every call "
+            "(counted in cudnn.triangle_attention.copy_counters()). Produce it in the zero-copy layout to avoid the copy.",
+            RuntimeWarning,
+            stacklevel=4,
+        )
+
+
+def _bshd_empty(b: int, n: int, h: int, s: int, d: int, dtype, device) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """A compact ``(B, N, S, H, D)`` allocation presented as ``(B, N, H, S, D)`` -- the kernels' zero-copy activation form."""
+    return torch.empty((b, n, s, h, d), dtype=dtype, device=device).permute(0, 1, 3, 2, 4)
+
+
+def _repack_activation(t: torch.Tensor, name: str, plan) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """A COUNTED copy of an activation into the compact token-major form."""
+    staged = _bshd_empty(*t.shape, t.dtype, t.device)
+    staged.copy_(t)
+    _count(
+        f"{name}_repack",
+        plan,
+        f"{name} with shape {tuple(t.shape)} and strides {tuple(t.stride())} is not in the (B, N, S, H, D) memory form (head dim contiguous, token-major, 16-byte strides)",
+    )
+    return staged
+
+
+def _repack_bias(bias: torch.Tensor, dtype: torch.dtype, plan) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """ONE counted copy that casts (fp32 -> the io dtype) and / or pads the key row to a multiple of 8 elements (the TMA 16-byte
+    row-stride rule) and makes the key dim contiguous."""
+    b, one, h, s_q, s_kv = bias.shape
+    pad = -(-s_kv // 8) * 8
+    staged = torch.empty((b, one, h, s_q, pad), dtype=dtype, device=bias.device)[..., :s_kv]
+    staged.copy_(bias)
+    if bias.dtype != dtype:
+        _count("bias_cast", plan, f"an {bias.dtype} bias is cast to the activations' dtype {dtype} (the engine loads the io dtype)")
+    else:
+        _count(
+            "bias_repack",
+            plan,
+            f"a bias with shape {tuple(bias.shape)} and strides {tuple(bias.stride())} needs a contiguous key dim and 16-byte row strides (S_kv % 8 == 0 or a padded row)",
+        )
+    return staged
+
+
+def _activation_zero_copy(t: torch.Tensor) -> bool:
+    shape4, stride4 = _row_strides(tuple(t.shape), tuple(t.stride()))
+    return activation_binds_zero_copy(shape4, stride4) and (t.shape[0] == 1 or (t.stride(0) * _ELEM_BYTES) % _TMA_ALIGN == 0)
+
+
+def _bias_zero_copy(bias: torch.Tensor, dtype: torch.dtype) -> bool:
+    shape4, stride4 = _row_strides(tuple(bias.shape), tuple(bias.stride()))
+    return bias.dtype == dtype and bias_binds_zero_copy(shape4, stride4) and (bias.shape[0] == 1 or (bias.stride(0) * _ELEM_BYTES) % _TMA_ALIGN == 0)
+
+
+def _cached_plan(q, k, v, bias, mask_form: str, want_lse: bool, score_max: bool, scale: float) -> TriangleAttentionFwd:
+    key = (
+        tuple(q.shape),
+        tuple(q.stride()),

**🎯 Functional Correctness** | **🟡 Minor** | **⚡ Quick win**

**Validate a caller-supplied `out` before `unsqueeze`, and squeeze only an output that the function allocated.**

A batchless `x` (`[N, N, c_z]`) can come with a 4-D `out` of shape `[1, N, N, c_z]`. `execute` accepts this `out`. Line 933 then returns `out4.squeeze(0)`, which is a 3-D view and not the caller's tensor shape. This case is minor.

There is a more important case. If `out` is a non-tensor or has the wrong number of dimensions, `out.ndim` fails before the typed `ValueError` in `_check_execute_args`. Also, `out` is checked for aliasing only by comparing `data_ptr`. That check misses partial overlap with `x`.

If `out` overlaps `x`, K3 reads `x` while it writes `out`. The result is then silently corrupted. Use a storage-overlap check (for example, `torch._C._overlaps` or a byte-range comparison) instead of exact pointer equality.

+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# The prepared API

+class TriangleMultiplicativeUpdateFwd(APIBase):
+    """Triangle multiplicative update, forward: one declaration, one workspace, three launches on one stream.

+    :class:`cudnn.api_base.TensorDesc`), the ``direction``, the hidden width ``c_hidden`` (= ``p_in_weight.shape[0] // 2``) and the
+    optional-tensor flags ``has_mask`` / ``has_in_bias`` / ``has_out_bias`` -- compile-time specialisations the execute arguments must match

+    SET axes override the measured pick for this geometry (an axis left ``None`` keeps the table's value: ``TriMulKnobs(clc_stages=4)`` changes

+    ``check_support``, the contraction tile's eligibility for this geometry probed there without a compile.

+        self.has_out_bias = bool(has_out_bias)
+        self.eps = float(eps)

+        # the contraction tile's eligibility probed there (NotImplementedError)

+        # CUDA device can be asked: the Rubin table; check_support then declines the device before any launch); the substrate body is
+        # resolved in check_support (``self.arch``)
+        self.cc = self._device_cc()
+        self.arch: Optional[str] = None
+        self.knobs = th.resolve(self.n_res, self.c, self.batch, direction, k2_tile=k2_tile, knobs=knobs, cc=self.cc)
+        self.k2_tile = self.knobs.k2_tile

+    def _device_cc(self) -> Optional[Tuple[int, int]]:

+    def check_support(self) -> bool:

+        if self.dtype != torch.bfloat16:

+        if c_z not in SUPPORTED_CHANNELS:

+            )
+        if c != c_z:
+            raise NotImplementedError(
+                f"triangle_multiplicative_update serves c_hidden == c_z today (one K for the output gate and projection GEMMs), got c_hidden={c}, c_z={c_z}"
+            )
+        if n < MIN_N_RES:
+            raise NotImplementedError(f"triangle_multiplicative_update needs N >= {MIN_N_RES} (the output stage's 64-row MN-major TMA box), got N={n}")
+        if self.direction == "incoming" and not k2.incoming_supported(n):
+            raise NotImplementedError(
+                f"the incoming direction needs N % {k2.CONTIGUOUS_EXTENT_MULTIPLE} == 0 today (the contraction reads MN-major operands whose contiguous "
+                f"extent is N, and a TMA-fed contiguous extent must be a multiple of 8 bf16 elements), got N={n}"
+            )
+        if b * n * n * c_z >= _INT32_MAX or 2 * c * b * n * self.n_pad >= _INT32_MAX:
+            raise NotImplementedError(
+                f"triangle_multiplicative_update addresses its tensors with 32-bit element offsets: B*N*N*c_z = {b * n * n * c_z} and the planes' "
+                f"2*c*B*N*n_pad = {2 * c * b * n * self.n_pad} must both stay below 2^31 = {_INT32_MAX}"
+            )
+        if self.device.type != "cuda":
+            raise ValueError(f"x must be a CUDA tensor, got device {self.device}")
+        index = self.device_index
+        cc = tuple(int(x) for x in torch.cuda.get_device_capability(index))
+        if cc not in _ARCHS_BY_CC:
+            served = ", ".join(f"{a}.{b}" for a, b in _SERVED_CCS)
+            raise NotImplementedError(
+                f"triangle_multiplicative_update is rendered for compute capabilities {served} (Blackwell SM100 / SM103, Rubin SM107) only today; found {cc[0]}.{cc[1]}"
+            )
+        self.cc = cc
+        self.arch = _body_arch_for_cc(cc)
+        # the two LayerNorm-prologue stages' records, validated against the BODY this device runs (the substrate's typed declines -- the per-arch K
+        # cap, the sm100 register-form class ptxas cannot allocate -- fire HERE, never inside compile()): a knob set the arch cannot serve is a
+        # NotImplementedError of this declaration, a malformed one stays the substrate's ValueError
+        from cudnn.gemm.frost.ln_prologue import validate_ln_dual_gemm_params as _validate_substrate
+
+        for stage_params in self._stage_params():
+            try:
+                _validate_substrate(stage_params, self.arch)
+            except ValueError as error:
+                raise NotImplementedError(
+                    f"triangle_multiplicative_update cannot serve this knob set on compute capability {cc[0]}.{cc[1]}: {error}"
+                ) from error
+        msg = cutedsl_requirement_error("triangle_multiplicative_update")
+        if msg:
+            raise NotImplementedError(msg)
+        msg = cutedsl_arch_requirement_error(cc)
+        if msg:
+            raise NotImplementedError(msg)
+        self._probe_contraction_tile()
+        self._is_supported = True
+        return True
+
+    def _probe_contraction_tile(self) -> None:
+        """The contraction tile's eligibility for THIS geometry on THIS device without a ``cute.compile`` (the FROST GEMM engine's own
+        ``check_support`` gates over the direction's operand majors, the folded ``c * B`` batch and the arch): a catalog name the engine
+        cannot run here is a typed ``NotImplementedError`` from ``check_support``, never a bare error inside ``compile()``."""
+        import cudnn
+        import cudnn.gemm.frost  # noqa: F401  -- the pygraph recorder hook the GEMM analyzer reads
+        from cudnn.gemm.frost.sm100.compiler import probe_supported
+        from cudnn.gemm.frost.tile_config import by_name
+
+        graph = k2.contraction_graph(cudnn, self.c, self.n_res, self.direction, batch=self.batch, padded=True)
+        try:
+            with torch.cuda.device(self.device_index):
+                probe_supported(graph, by_name(self.k2_tile))
+        except NotImplementedError:
+            raise
+        except Exception as error:  # the engine's untyped refusals (a synthesized name's geometry, a template gate) become the typed decline
+            raise NotImplementedError(
+                f"the contraction tile config {self.k2_tile!r} cannot serve the {self.direction} contraction at N={self.n_res}, c={self.c}, B={self.batch} "
+                f"on this device: {type(error).__name__}: {error}"
+            ) from error
+
+    @property
+    def device_index(self) -> int:
+        """The declaration's CUDA device index (``torch.cuda.current_device()`` when the declaration named ``cuda`` without an index)."""
+        return self.device.index if self.device.index is not None else torch.cuda.current_device()
+
+    # -- workspace ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+    @property
+    def planes_shape(self) -> Tuple[int, int, int, int]:
+        return k1.planes_shape(self.c, self.batch, self.n_res)
+
+    @property
+    def y_shape(self) -> Tuple[int, int, int]:
+        return k3.y_shape(self.c, self.batch, self.n_res)
+
+    def _planes_bytes(self) -> int:
+        p = self.planes_shape
+        return _align_up(2 * p[0] * p[1] * p[2] * p[3])
+
+    def _y_bytes(self) -> int:
+        y = self.y_shape
+        return _align_up(2 * y[0] * y[1] * y[2])
+
+    def _slack_bytes(self) -> int:
+        """The readable tail after the ``b`` plane the outgoing contraction over-reads at ``N % 8 != 0`` (:func:`k2.k2_slack_bytes`)."""
+        return _align_up(k2.k2_slack_bytes(self.n_res)) if self.direction == "outgoing" else 0
+
+    def get_workspace_size(self) -> int:
+        """Bytes of the one workspace ``execute`` carves: the two channel-major planes ``a``, ``b`` (plus the contraction's over-read slack
+        at ``N % 8 != 0``) and the contraction output ``y`` (bf16, the inner axis padded to a multiple of 8), each 256-byte aligned."""
+        return self._planes_bytes() + self._slack_bytes() + self._y_bytes()
+
+    def traffic_bytes(self) -> int:
+        """The compulsory HBM traffic model of one call: ``18 N^2 C`` bytes per batch entry plus the mask (2 B per pair) -- read against the
+        measured figure in the documentation."""
+        return (
+            k1.proj_bytes(self.c_z, self.c, self.batch, self.n_res, with_mask=self.has_mask, with_stats=False)
+            + k2.contraction_bytes(self.c, self.n_res, batch=self.batch)
+            + k3.tail_bytes(self.c_z, self.c, self.batch, self.n_res, with_stats=False)
+        )
+
+    def flop(self) -> int:
+        return (
+            k1.proj_flop(self.c_z, self.c, self.batch, self.n_res)
+            + k2.contraction_flop(self.c, self.n_res, batch=self.batch)
+            + k3.tail_flop(self.c_z, self.c, self.batch, self.n_res)
+        )
+
+    # -- compile ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+    def _k3_ln_pass_form(self) -> str:
+        # the re-read LayerNorm forms re-read the MN-major operand in every pass, which the transpose prologue's K-major writes would overwrite
+        # (a typed decline of the substrate): under `transpose` the output stage keeps the register form and the knob's value serves the
+        # projection stage alone
+        return self.knobs.ln_pass_form if self.knobs.k3_prologue == "mn_major" else "registers"
+
+    def _k3_ln_once(self) -> str:
+        """The output stage's LayerNorm-once work item: the knob's value where the item spans at least two GEMM tiles there (one pass, so
+        ``"block"`` at two N tiles = c = 256), else today's per-tile item -- the substrate declines a one-tile item (K3 at c = 128; ``"passes"``
+        under one pass), so the knob's value serves the projection stage alone on those plans.  GPU-free (pinned by the API tests)."""
+        form = self.knobs.ln_once or ""
+        if not form:
+            return ""
+        trial = k3.tail_params(self.c_z, self.c, has_bias=self.has_out_bias, want_stats=False, a0_prologue=self.knobs.k3_prologue, ln_once=form)
+        return form if _ln_once_tiles_per_item(trial) >= 2 else ""
+
+    def _register_split_hints(self) -> Tuple[int, int]:
+        """The `.minnctapersm` launch hint of (K1, K3): the caller's `min_blocks_per_mp` override for both stages, else the per-RENDERING rule with
+        each stage's own bias flag, LayerNorm form, (K1) tile order and LayerNorm work item (`heuristics.register_split_hint`: whether a rendering
+        spills at the flat allocation is a property of the rendering, not of the geometry -- and the LayerNorm-once item's rendering spills UNDER
+        the hint where the per-tile item's did without it, so the rows name the per-tile item); the width is the heuristics' (`c`, = `c_z` on every
+        served plan).  GPU-free (pinned by the API tests)."""
+        hint = self.knobs.min_blocks_per_mp
+        if hint is not None:
+            return int(hint), int(hint)
+        return (
+            th.register_split_hint(
+                "k1", self.c, self.has_in_bias, self.knobs.ln_pass_form, self.knobs.epi_math, self.knobs.k1_pass_order, self.knobs.ln_once or "", cc=self.cc
+            ),
+            th.register_split_hint("k3", self.c, self.has_out_bias, self._k3_ln_pass_form(), self.knobs.epi_math, None, self._k3_ln_once(), cc=self.cc),
+        )
+
+    def _stage_params(self):
+        """The (K1, K3) substrate records this declaration compiles -- ONE builder for ``check_support`` (validated against the arch body) and
+        ``compile`` (built), so a decline and a build can never disagree on the record.  GPU-free."""
+        k3_ln_pass_form = self._k3_ln_pass_form()
+        k1_hint, k3_hint = self._register_split_hints()
+        k1_ln_once, k3_ln_once = self.knobs.ln_once or "", self._k3_ln_once()
+        return (
+            k1.proj_params(
+                self.c_z,
+                self.c,
+                has_bias=self.has_in_bias,
+                has_mask=self.has_mask,
+                want_stats=False,
+                eps=self.eps,
+                pass_order=self.knobs.k1_pass_order,
+                clc_stages=self.knobs.clc_stages,
+                ln_pass_form=self.knobs.ln_pass_form,
+                epi_math=self.knobs.epi_math,
+                min_blocks_per_mp=k1_hint,
+                ln_once=k1_ln_once,
+                ln_once_b_stages=(self.knobs.ln_once_b_stages or 0) if k1_ln_once else 0,
+            ),
+            k3.tail_params(
+                self.c_z,
+                self.c,
+                has_bias=self.has_out_bias,
+                want_stats=False,
+                eps=self.eps,
+                a0_prologue=self.knobs.k3_prologue,
+                clc_stages=self.knobs.clc_stages,
+                ln_pass_form=k3_ln_pass_form,
+                epi_math=self.knobs.epi_math,
+                min_blocks_per_mp=k3_hint,
+                ln_once=k3_ln_once,
+                ln_once_b_stages=(self.knobs.ln_once_b_stages or 0) if k3_ln_once else 0,
+            ),
+        )
+
+    def compile(self) -> None:
+        """Build the three plans: K1 (the columns arm of the substrate), K2 (the FROST GEMM engine's dense template for the per-N tile over the
+        folded ``c * B`` batch), K3 (the accumulators arm).  Each is cached on its parameter set; a second instance of the same declaration
+        reuses them."""
+        self._ensure_support_checked()
+        import cudnn
+        import cudnn.gemm.frost  # noqa: F401  -- installs the pygraph recorder hook the GEMM compiler reads
+
+        # Compile and load on the PLAN's device: the declaration may name a device other than torch's current one (a multi-GPU host with
+        # ``x`` on ``cuda:1``).  A compiled launchable is bound to the context it was loaded in, so K1 / K3 and K2 are cached per
+        # (parameter set, arch body, device) -- :func:`_substrate_plan_on`, :func:`_compile_contraction`.
+        k1_params, k3_params = self._stage_params()
+        arch = self.arch if self.arch is not None else _body_arch_for_cc(self.cc)
+        with torch.cuda.device(self.device_index):
+            self._plan_k1 = _substrate_plan_on(k1.build_trimul_proj, k1_params, self.device_index, arch)
+            self._plan_k3 = _substrate_plan_on(k3.build_trimul_tail, k3_params, self.device_index, arch)
+            self._k2 = _compile_contraction(cudnn, self.c, self.batch, self.n_res, self.direction, self.k2_tile, self.device_index)
+        self._k2_binding = self._k2.binding
+        self._compiled_kernel = (self._plan_k1, self._k2, self._plan_k3)
+
+    # -- execute ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+    def _check_execute_args(self, x, mask, weights, out, workspace) -> None:
+        b, n, c_z, c = self.batch, self.n_res, self.c_z, self.c
+        bf16 = torch.bfloat16
+        if isinstance(weights, TriMulWeights):
+            _autograd_decline(
+                [("x", x), ("mask", mask), ("out", out)]
+                + [
+                    (f"weights.{f}", getattr(weights, f))
+                    for f in ("w_in", "b_in", "norm_in_weight", "norm_in_bias", "norm_out_weight", "norm_out_bias", "p_out_weight", "g_out_weight", "b_out")
+                ]
+            )
+        else:
+            _autograd_decline([("x", x), ("mask", mask), ("out", out)])
+        # the PLAN's device first: its kernels are loaded on cuda:<device_index> and launched there -- tensors on another device would pass
+        # every shape check below and hand foreign pointers to kernels running on the wrong GPU
+        if self.device.type == "cuda" and (not isinstance(x, torch.Tensor) or x.device.type != "cuda" or x.device.index != self.device_index):
+            raise ValueError(
+                f"x lives on {getattr(x, 'device', None)}; this plan was declared on cuda:{self.device_index} and its kernels are loaded there "
+                "(declare and compile one plan per device)"
+            )
+        if not isinstance(x, torch.Tensor) or x.dtype != bf16 or not x.is_contiguous() or tuple(x.shape) != (b, n, n, c_z):
+            raise ValueError(
+                f"x must be a contiguous bf16 [{b}, {n}, {n}, {c_z}] tensor (the declaration), got {getattr(x, 'shape', None)} {getattr(x, 'dtype', None)}"
+            )
+        if not isinstance(out, torch.Tensor) or out.dtype != bf16 or not out.is_contiguous() or tuple(out.shape) != (b, n, n, c_z):
+            raise ValueError(f"out must be a contiguous bf16 [{b}, {n}, {n}, {c_z}] tensor, got {getattr(out, 'shape', None)} {getattr(out, 'dtype', None)}")
+        if self.has_mask:
+            if mask is None:
+                raise ValueError("this plan was compiled with has_mask=True; a bf16 [B, N, N] mask must be passed (no silent all-valid fallback)")
+            if mask.dtype != bf16 or not mask.is_contiguous() or tuple(mask.shape) != (b, n, n):
+                raise ValueError(f"mask must be a contiguous bf16 [{b}, {n}, {n}] tensor, got {tuple(mask.shape)} {mask.dtype}")
+        elif mask is not None:
+            raise ValueError("this plan was compiled with has_mask=False; mask must be None (compile a plan with has_mask=True to apply one)")
+        if not isinstance(weights, TriMulWeights):
+            raise TypeError("weights must be a TriMulWeights (prepare_weights(...)); the kernels take the interleaved layouts, prepared once")
+        if (weights.c_z, weights.c) != (c_z, c):
+            raise ValueError(f"weights were prepared for (c_z, c) = {(weights.c_z, weights.c)}, the plan for {(c_z, c)}")
+        if weights.has_in_bias != self.has_in_bias:
+            raise ValueError(f"this plan was compiled with has_in_bias={self.has_in_bias}; the weights carry an input bias: {weights.has_in_bias}")
+        if weights.has_out_bias != self.has_out_bias:
+            raise ValueError(f"this plan was compiled with has_out_bias={self.has_out_bias}; the weights carry an output bias: {weights.has_out_bias}")
+        if (
+            not isinstance(workspace, torch.Tensor)
+            or workspace.dtype != torch.uint8
+            or workspace.numel() < self.get_workspace_size()
+            or not workspace.is_contiguous()
+        ):
+            raise ValueError(f"workspace must be a contiguous uint8 tensor of at least get_workspace_size() = {self.get_workspace_size()} bytes")
+        for name, t in (("x", x), ("out", out), ("workspace", workspace), ("mask", mask)):
+            if t is not None and t.device != x.device:
+                raise ValueError(f"{name} must live on x's device {x.device}, got {t.device}")
+        if weights.device != x.device:
+            raise ValueError(f"weights must live on x's device {x.device}, got {weights.device}")
+        if workspace.data_ptr() % _WS_ALIGN:
+            raise ValueError(f"workspace must be {_WS_ALIGN}-byte aligned")
+        if out.data_ptr() == x.data_ptr():
+            raise ValueError("out must not alias x (the output stage reads x while it writes out)")
+
+    def _carve(self, workspace: torch.Tensor):
+        """``(plane_a, plane_b, y)`` views over the workspace (no allocation)."""
+        p = self.planes_shape
+        planes = workspace[: 2 * p[0] * p[1] * p[2] * p[3]].view(torch.bfloat16).view(*p)
+        yb = self._y_bytes()
+        y_off = self._planes_bytes() + self._slack_bytes()
+        y = workspace[y_off : y_off + yb][: 2 * self.y_shape[0] * self.y_shape[1] * self.y_shape[2]].view(torch.bfloat16).view(*self.y_shape)
+        return planes, planes[0], planes[1], y
+
+    def execute(self, x, mask, weights, out, workspace, current_stream: Optional[cuda.CUstream] = None) -> None:
+        """Launch K1, K2, K3 on ``current_stream`` (None = torch's current stream on the plan's device).  Validates, never converts or
+        allocates.  The launches run with the plan's device current (``torch.cuda.device`` -- a context switch, no synchronisation), so a
+        plan declared on ``cuda:1`` is served from any current device."""
+        if self._compiled_kernel is None:
+            raise RuntimeError("compile() must run before execute()")
+        self._check_execute_args(x, mask, weights, out, workspace)
+        stream = _stream_handle(current_stream, self.device)
+        with torch.cuda.device(self.device_index):
+            self._launch(x, mask, weights, out, workspace, stream)
+
+    def _launch(self, x, mask, weights, out, workspace, stream: int) -> None:
+        planes, plane_a, plane_b, y = self._carve(workspace)
+        b, n, c_z = self.batch, self.n_res, self.c_z
+        k1.run_trimul_proj(
+            self._plan_k1,
+            x,
+            weights.w_in,
+            planes,
+            weights.norm_in_weight,
+            weights.norm_in_bias,
+            bias_stacked=weights.b_in,
+            mask=mask,
+            stats=None,
+            stream=stream,
+            k_block=self.knobs.k_block,
+        )
+        a_v, b_v, y_v = k2.k2_operand_views(plane_a, plane_b, y, channels=self.c, batch=b, n_res=n, direction=self.direction)
+        bd = self._k2_binding
+        self._k2({bd.a_operands[0]: a_v, bd.b_operands[0]: b_v, bd.outputs[0]: y_v}, stream=stream)
+        k3.run_trimul_tail(
+            self._plan_k3,
+            y,
+            x,
+            weights.p_out_weight,
+            weights.g_out_weight,
+            out,
+            weights.norm_out_weight,
+            weights.norm_out_bias,
+            weights.norm_in_weight,
+            weights.norm_in_bias,
+            biases=weights.b_out,
+            stats=None,
+            residual=None,
+            stream=stream,
+            k_block=self.knobs.k_block,
+        )
+
+    def make_cuda_graph(self, x, mask, weights, out, workspace, *, warmup: int = 2) -> "torch.cuda.CUDAGraph":
+        """Capture the three launches for THESE buffers into one ``torch.cuda.CUDAGraph`` (replay = one graph launch per call; the
+        buffers' contents may change between replays, their addresses may not).  ``warmup`` eager calls run first on a side stream."""
+        side = torch.cuda.Stream(device=x.device)
+        side.wait_stream(torch.cuda.current_stream(x.device))
+        with torch.cuda.stream(side):
+            for _ in range(int(warmup)):
+                self.execute(x, mask, weights, out, workspace, current_stream=cuda.CUstream(side.cuda_stream))
+        torch.cuda.current_stream(x.device).wait_stream(side)
+        torch.cuda.synchronize(x.device)
+        graph = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
+        with torch.cuda.graph(graph, stream=side):
+            self.execute(x, mask, weights, out, workspace, current_stream=cuda.CUstream(side.cuda_stream))
+        return graph
+
+
+_K2_LOCK = threading.Lock()
+_K2_CACHE: Dict[Tuple[Any, ...], Any] = {}
+_SUBSTRATE_LOCK = threading.Lock()
+_SUBSTRATE_PLANS: Dict[Tuple[Any, int], Any] = {}
+
+
+def _substrate_plan_on(build, params, device_index: int, arch: str = "sm107"):
+    """One cute-compiled launchable of the K1 / K3 substrate per (parameter set, arch body, device).  A CuTe-DSL launchable is bound to the CUDA
+    context it was first loaded in -- a K1 launchable built on ``cuda:0`` fails on ``cuda:1`` with ``cudaErrorInvalidValue`` at launch, and
+    vice versa (measured on a two-GPU host) -- while the substrate's ``build_*`` cache is per parameter set only.  Under the plan's device:
+    when the substrate's cache fills NOW its launchable is bound here and is reused (the single-device case pays nothing extra); when it was
+    filled earlier -- by a plan on another device, or by a caller outside this API -- the same template module gets a second ``cute.compile``
+    for this device, cached per (params, device)."""
+    from cudnn.gemm.frost import ln_prologue
+
+    key = (params, str(arch), int(device_index))
+    with _SUBSTRATE_LOCK:
+        hit = _SUBSTRATE_PLANS.get(key)
+    if hit is not None:
+        return hit
+    with torch.cuda.device(device_index), _SUBSTRATE_LOCK:
+        before = ln_prologue.build_ln_dual_gemm.cache_info().currsize
+        base = build(params, arch)
+        built_here = ln_prologue.build_ln_dual_gemm.cache_info().currsize > before
+        plan = base if built_here else ln_prologue.LnDualGemmPlan(params=base.params, module=base.module, launch=base.module.compile.__wrapped__())
+        return _SUBSTRATE_PLANS.setdefault(key, plan)
+
+
+def _compile_contraction(cudnn_module, channels: int, batch: int, n_res: int, direction: str, tile: str, device_index: int):
+    """The compiled FROST GEMM instance of the contraction for ``(c * B, direction, tile, dtype, device)`` -- M / N / K are symbolic in the
+    kernel, the batch count is baked, so the cache key is the folded batch, not N.  Keyed on the PLAN's device (not the current one): the
+    caller enters ``torch.cuda.device(device_index)`` around the compile, so a plan for ``cuda:1`` never binds a module loaded on ``cuda:0``."""
+    from cudnn.gemm.frost.compiler import jit_from_cudnn_graph
+    from cudnn.gemm.frost.tile_config import by_name
+
+    index = int(device_index)
+    key = (channels * batch, direction, tile, "bf16", index)
+    with _K2_LOCK:
+        hit = _K2_CACHE.get(key)
+        if hit is not None:
+            return hit
+    graph = k2.contraction_graph(cudnn_module, channels, n_res, direction, batch=batch, padded=True)
+    compiled = jit_from_cudnn_graph(graph, config=by_name(tile))
+    with _K2_LOCK:
+        return _K2_CACHE.setdefault(key, compiled)
+
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# The drop-in function (cuEquivariance's signature)
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+_PLAN_LOCK = threading.Lock()
+_PLANS: Dict[Tuple[Any, ...], TriangleMultiplicativeUpdateFwd] = {}
+_WEIGHTS: "OrderedDict[Tuple[Any, ...], Tuple[TriMulWeights, tuple]]" = OrderedDict()
+_WEIGHTS_MAX = 8
+
+_PRECISION_DEFAULT = ("NONE", "DEFAULT")
+_PRECISION_BF16 = ("BF16", "BFLOAT16")
+
+
+def _parse_precision(precision) -> str:
+    """cuEquivariance's ``precision`` spellings -> ``"default"`` (bf16 inputs required) or ``"bfloat16"`` (cast wider inputs); the
+    rest (``"mxfp8"``, ``"ieee"``, ``"tf32"``, ...) are typed declines."""
+    if precision is None:
+        return "default"
+    name = None
+    if isinstance(precision, str):
+        name = precision.upper()
+    elif isinstance(precision, int) and not isinstance(precision, bool):
+        name = {-1: "NONE", 0: "DEFAULT", 5: "BFLOAT16", 4: "MXFP8", 3: "IEEE", 1: "TF32", 2: "TF32X3"}.get(precision, str(precision))
+    elif hasattr(precision, "name"):
+        name = str(precision.name).upper()
+    else:
+        raise ValueError(f"precision must be None, a string or a cuEquivariance Precision, got {type(precision).__name__}")
+    if name in _PRECISION_DEFAULT:
+        return "default"
+    if name in _PRECISION_BF16:
+        return "bfloat16"
+    if name == "MXFP8":
+        raise NotImplementedError("precision='mxfp8' (block-scaled a / b operands) is not served by triangle_multiplicative_update yet")
+    raise NotImplementedError(f"precision={precision!r} is not served by triangle_multiplicative_update (bf16 arithmetic only: None / 'default' / 'bfloat16')")
+
+
+def _tensor_identity(t: Optional[torch.Tensor]):
+    if t is None:
+        return None
+    return (t.data_ptr(), t.storage_offset(), tuple(t.shape), tuple(t.stride()), t.dtype, str(t.device), t._version)
+
+
+def _cached_weights(params: tuple, cast: bool) -> TriMulWeights:
+    """One prepared weight set per PARAMETER IDENTITY (address, shape, strides, dtype, device and torch's in-place version counter
+    of each of the twelve tensors); the entry keeps a reference to the source tensors so an address cannot be recycled under it.
+    A bounded LRU: a model switches parameter sets rarely, a training loop bumps the version counter and misses (one re-interleave)."""
+    key = (cast,) + tuple(_tensor_identity(t) for t in params)
+    with _PLAN_LOCK:
+        hit = _WEIGHTS.get(key)
+        if hit is not None:
+            _WEIGHTS.move_to_end(key)
+            return hit[0]
+    prepared = prepare_weights(*params, cast_to_bf16=cast)
+    with _PLAN_LOCK:
+        _WEIGHTS[key] = (prepared, tuple(t for t in params if t is not None))
+        _WEIGHTS.move_to_end(key)
+        while len(_WEIGHTS) > _WEIGHTS_MAX:
+            _WEIGHTS.popitem(last=False)
+    return prepared
+
+
+def _cached_plan(x: torch.Tensor, direction: str, c: int, has_mask: bool, has_in_bias: bool, has_out_bias: bool, eps: float) -> TriangleMultiplicativeUpdateFwd:
+    key = (tuple(x.shape), x.dtype, str(x.device), direction, int(c), bool(has_mask), bool(has_in_bias), bool(has_out_bias), float(eps))
+    with _PLAN_LOCK:
+        plan = _PLANS.get(key)
+    if plan is not None:
+        return plan
+    plan = TriangleMultiplicativeUpdateFwd(x, direction, c_hidden=c, has_mask=has_mask, has_in_bias=has_in_bias, has_out_bias=has_out_bias, eps=eps)
+    plan.check_support()
+    plan.compile()
+    with _PLAN_LOCK:
+        return _PLANS.setdefault(key, plan)
+
+
+def triangle_multiplicative_update(
+    x: torch.Tensor,
+    direction: str = "outgoing",
+    mask: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None,
+    norm_in_weight: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None,
+    norm_in_bias: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None,
+    p_in_weight: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None,
+    p_in_bias: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None,
+    g_in_weight: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None,
+    g_in_bias: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None,
+    norm_out_weight: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None,
+    norm_out_bias: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None,
+    p_out_weight: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None,
+    p_out_bias: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None,
+    g_out_weight: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None,
+    g_out_bias: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None,
+    eps: float = 1e-5,
+    precision=None,
+    *,
+    out: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None,
+    stream=None,
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """The triangle multiplicative update of ``x`` (``[B, N, N, c_z]`` or ``[N, N, c_z]`` bf16) -- cuEquivariance's signature
+    (``cuequivariance_ops_torch.triangle_multiplicative_update``, 0.12.0) with two keyword-only additions: ``out`` (write into this
+    bf16 tensor instead of allocating) and ``stream`` (a raw CUDA stream handle the allocations and launches are ordered on; None = torch's
+    current stream).  Returns the update (the caller adds the residual), shaped like ``x``.
+
+    Differences from cuEquivariance, all typed: the eight weights are REQUIRED (no implicit random initialisation); ``precision`` is
+    None / ``'default'`` (bf16 inputs required) or ``'bfloat16'`` (wider inputs cast once per call, as cuEquivariance does), ``'mxfp8'`` and
+    the IEEE / TF32 modes decline; a non-contiguous ``x`` declines; autograd is not registered yet, so under grad mode an input or
+    parameter with ``requires_grad`` is a typed decline (``NotImplementedError``), never a tensor without a ``grad_fn`` -- call under
+    ``torch.no_grad()`` or detach for inference.  A mask of any real or bool dtype is cast once per call to the kernels' bf16 ``[B, N, N]`` (no copy when
+    it already is).  One compiled plan per (shape, direction, flags) and one prepared weight set per parameter identity are cached in
+    the process; warm a shape before capturing a CUDA graph around this call.
+    """
+    from cudnn._torch_stream import stream_context
+
+    if direction not in DIRECTIONS:
+        raise ValueError(f"direction must be one of {DIRECTIONS}, got {direction!r}")
+    mode = _parse_precision(precision)
+    cast = mode == "bfloat16"
+    if not isinstance(x, torch.Tensor):
+        raise TypeError(f"x must be a torch.Tensor, got {type(x).__name__}")
+    squeeze = x.ndim == 3
+    x4 = x.unsqueeze(0) if squeeze else x
+    if x4.ndim != 4 or x4.shape[1] != x4.shape[2]:
+        raise ValueError(f"x must be [B, N, N, c_z] or [N, N, c_z], got {tuple(x.shape)}")
+    if p_in_weight is None or p_in_weight.ndim != 2 or p_in_weight.shape[0] % 2:
+        raise ValueError("p_in_weight is required and must be [2 c, c_z] (rows [a; b])")
+    for name, w in (
+        ("norm_in_weight", norm_in_weight),
+        ("norm_in_bias", norm_in_bias),
+        ("g_in_weight", g_in_weight),
+        ("norm_out_weight", norm_out_weight),
+        ("norm_out_bias", norm_out_bias),
+        ("p_out_weight", p_out_weight),
+        ("g_out_weight", g_out_weight),
+    ):
+        if w is None:
+            raise ValueError(f"{name} is required (this API never initialises parameters implicitly)")
+    c = int(p_in_weight.shape[0]) // 2
+    _autograd_decline(
+        [
+            ("x", x),
+            ("mask", mask),
+            ("norm_in_weight", norm_in_weight),
+            ("norm_in_bias", norm_in_bias),
+            ("p_in_weight", p_in_weight),
+            ("p_in_bias", p_in_bias),
+            ("g_in_weight", g_in_weight),
+            ("g_in_bias", g_in_bias),
+            ("norm_out_weight", norm_out_weight),
+            ("norm_out_bias", norm_out_bias),
+            ("p_out_weight", p_out_weight),
+            ("p_out_bias", p_out_bias),
+            ("g_out_weight", g_out_weight),
+            ("g_out_bias", g_out_bias),
+            ("out", out),
+        ]
+    )
+    device = x4.device
+    with stream_context(stream, device):
+        if x4.dtype != torch.bfloat16:
+            if not cast:
+                raise NotImplementedError(
+                    f"triangle_multiplicative_update serves bf16 pair representations only (got {x4.dtype}); pass precision='bfloat16' to cast like cuEquivariance"
+                )
+            x4 = x4.to(torch.bfloat16)
+        if not x4.is_contiguous():
+            raise ValueError("x must be contiguous ([B, N, N, c_z] row-major); the kernels read it natively and never repack")
+        batch, n_res = int(x4.shape[0]), int(x4.shape[1])
+        m = None
+        if mask is not None:
+            m = mask.unsqueeze(0) if mask.ndim == 2 else mask
+            if m.ndim != 3 or tuple(m.shape) != (batch, n_res, n_res):
+                raise ValueError(f"mask must be [B, N, N] = {(batch, n_res, n_res)} (or [N, N] for B = 1), got {tuple(mask.shape)}")
+            if m.dtype != torch.bfloat16:
+                m = m.to(torch.bfloat16)  # bool / fp32 masks: cast once per call (cuEquivariance's path too)
+            if not m.is_contiguous():
+                m = m.contiguous()
+        has_in_bias = p_in_bias is not None or g_in_bias is not None
+        has_out_bias = p_out_bias is not None or g_out_bias is not None
+        # the plan first: its typed declines (width, N, direction, arch) must fire before any parameter is touched
+        plan = _cached_plan(x4, direction, c, m is not None, has_in_bias, has_out_bias, float(eps))
+        weights = _cached_weights(
+            (
+                norm_in_weight,
+                norm_in_bias,
+                p_in_weight,
+                p_in_bias,
+                g_in_weight,
+                g_in_bias,
+                norm_out_weight,
+                norm_out_bias,
+                p_out_weight,
+                p_out_bias,
+                g_out_weight,
+                g_out_bias,
+            ),
+            cast,
+        )
+        if out is None:
+            out4 = torch.empty_like(x4)
+        else:
+            out4 = out.unsqueeze(0) if out.ndim == 3 else out
+        workspace = torch.empty(plan.get_workspace_size(), dtype=torch.uint8, device=device)
+        plan.execute(x4, m, weights, out4, workspace, current_stream=cuda.CUstream(_stream_handle(stream, device)))
+    return out4.squeeze(0) if squeeze else out4

+                has_bias=self.bias_desc is not None,

+                kv_mask_fp32=self.kv_mask_desc is not None and self.kv_mask_desc.dtype == torch.float32,

+    def _resident_arm_cga(self) -> int:

+        ``check_support`` then declines with the budget.  Read by ``check_support`` and ``template_params`` alike.
+        The pair item's 128-row block is evaluated at cga1 when the plan qualifies for it (``_resident_arm_pair_eligible``)."""

+            return int(self.cga)

+            if self.flavor not in _SM100_BIAS_D_SHAPES:

+            return _sm100_bias_auto_cga(self.flavor[0], int(self.k_desc.shape[2]), _SM100_SMALL_D_CGAS[self.flavor], tile_n=self._effective_tile_n()) or 1

+            return 1
+        return (
+            _sm107_bias_auto_cga(
+                self.flavor[0],
+                int(self.k_desc.shape[2]),

+                tiles_q=self._resident_arm_softmax_wgs(),

+            or 1
+        )

+    def _resident_arm_n_chunk(self) -> int:

+        if not self._resident_arm_pair_eligible() or self._resident_arm_cga() != 1:
+            return 0

+            return int(self.n_chunk)

+        return _sm107_n_chunk_pick(

+    def _resident_arm_bias_mode(self) -> int:

+        global lengths (``_kv_padded`` False: real per-batch lengths, or a dense S_kv tail the plan masks against the scalar S_kv,
+        keep the cga1 ring) and the NATURAL scheduler; 0 = no form fits --

+            # width (config_sm100.sm100_bias_mode_pick) when it is the resident block, else 0 (check_support declines typed; a ring REQUEST
+            # is declined by name there).

+            # per-batch lengths, and the NATURAL scheduler (a None policy derives to NATURAL on this device, template_params below)

+    def _s_slots(self) -> int:

+    def _resident_arm_softmax_wgs(self) -> int:

+        pair predicate it reads does not read the width or the chunk pick back (no cycle); ``_s_slots`` reads the width only (no cycle either)."""

+            d_flavor=self.flavor[0],
+            s_kv=int(self.k_desc.shape[2]),
+            tile_n=self._effective_tile_n(),
+            pair=self._resident_arm_pair_eligible(),
+            has_bias=True,
+            has_kv_mask=self.kv_mask_desc is not None,
+            padded=self._kv_padded(),

+            b_flat=int(self.q_desc.shape[0]),

+        )

+    def _padded_tail_form_eligible(self) -> bool:

+            # and the small-tile factory refuses a decode record.
+            return (

+                and self.flavor in _SM100_BIAS_D_SHAPES
+                and bool(self.seq_kv_lens_present)
+                and not self.thd
+                and self.kv_mask_desc is None
+                and not self.is_causal
+                and self.window_size_left is None
+                and self.window_size_right is None
+                and not self._d64_decode_tile()
+            )

+                softmax_wgs=self._resident_arm_softmax_wgs(),
+                # the cta_mma arm of template_params(): a bias plan takes the heuristics' width, a plan without one its request or the tiles' cga1
+                cta_mma=self._resident_arm_cga() if self.bias_desc is not None else (int(self.cga) if self.cga is not None else 1),
+                # the Q tile height the factory renders (128, or 64 under the TILE_M sweep seam): the same resolver the budgets read
+                tile_m=_sm107_tile_m_d128(self.flavor[0]),
+                seq_kv_lens_present=bool(self.seq_kv_lens_present),
+                dense_unsplit=not (self.thd or int(self.split_kv) > 1 or self.pack_gqa or self.gate_desc is not None),
+            )
+        return 0
+
+    def _resident_arm_bias_stages(self) -> int:
+        """The ``TemplateParams.bias_stages`` of this plan: 0 off the streamed ring; else the request (``bias_stages=``, validated by
+        ``check_support``) or the derived deepest ring (``config_sm107.sm107_bias_stages_pick``)."""
+        if self._resident_arm_bias_mode() not in _BIAS_STREAMED_MODES:
+            return 0
+        _cga = self._resident_arm_cga()
+        if self._device_cc != (10, 7):
+            # The SM100 line: the derived deepest ring at this width (config_sm100.sm100_bias_stages_pick; 2 at the 32-wide tile's
+            # one-batch-entry item), the request when it fits.
+            return _sm100_bias_stages_pick(self.flavor[0], _cga, tile_n=self._effective_tile_n(), request=self.bias_stages or 0)
+        return _sm107_bias_stages_pick(
+            self.flavor[0],
+            _cga,
+            pair=self._resident_arm_pair_eligible() and _cga == 1,
+            request=self.bias_stages or 0,
+            tiles_q=self._resident_arm_softmax_wgs(),
+        )
+
+    def _resident_arm_softmax_wgs(self) -> int:
+        """The ``TemplateParams.softmax_wgs`` of this plan: the request (``softmax_wgs=``, validated by ``check_support``), else the sweep seam,
+        else the measured rule (``config_sm107.sm107_softmax_wgs_pick``: 3 for a bias + kv_mask graph on the pair item at tile_n 64 / cga 1 with
+        dense KV lengths at ``s_kv >= SM107_THREE_WG_S_KV_MIN``, 2 everywhere else).  Threaded as ``tiles_q`` into every bias budget / pick this
+        plan evaluates (the 3-WG body's third Q and O slab shrink the SMEM left for the bias block) and as ``rows_per_step`` into the chunk pick,
+        so the plan is admitted on the budget of the body that RUNS and its chunk is a multiple of the body's rows per step (rule 8b').  The
+        pair predicate it reads does not read the width or the chunk pick back (no cycle); ``_s_slots`` reads the width only (no cycle either)."""
+        if self.bias_desc is None:
+            return _sm107_softmax_wgs_pick(self.softmax_wgs, s_slots=self._s_slots())
+        return _sm107_softmax_wgs_pick(
+            self.softmax_wgs,
+            d_flavor=self.flavor[0],
+            s_kv=int(self.k_desc.shape[2]),
+            tile_n=self._effective_tile_n(),
+            pair=self._resident_arm_pair_eligible(),
+            has_bias=True,
+            has_kv_mask=self.kv_mask_desc is not None,
+            padded=self._kv_padded(),
+            cga=1 if self.cga is None else int(self.cga),
+            b_flat=int(self.q_desc.shape[0]),
+            s_slots=self._s_slots(),  # a two-slot record is served with two groups only (the pick degrades its default; a request stays typed)
+        )
+
+    def _padded_tail_form_eligible(self) -> bool:
+        """Whether this plan runs the Rubin small tiles' PLAIN padded body (MASK_FLAGS == MASK_PADDED alone): the only rendering with a
+        padded tail form to choose (``TemplateParams.padded_tail_form``)."""
+        if self._device_cc in _SM100_BIAS_CCS:
+            # The SM100 small tiles' padded body WITHOUT a kv_mask -- the plain body, or the bias body (whose -inf loop renders at MASK_NONE under
+            # the pre-masked tail); a d64 plan the DECODE tile would take (S_q <= 128 at cga1) is not eligible: the decode tile has no tail form
+            # and the small-tile factory refuses a decode record.
+            return (
+                not self._fp8
+                and self.flavor in _SM100_BIAS_D_SHAPES
+                and bool(self.seq_kv_lens_present)
+                and not self.thd
+                and self.kv_mask_desc is None
+                and not self.is_causal
+                and self.window_size_left is None
+                and self.window_size_right is None
+                and not self._d64_decode_tile()
+            )
+        return (
+            self._device_cc == (10, 7)
+            and not self._fp8
+            and self.flavor in _SM107_F16_SMALL_D_SHAPES
+            and self._kv_padded()
+            and not self.thd
+            and self.bias_desc is None
+            and self.kv_mask_desc is None
+            and not self.is_causal
+            and self.window_size_left is None
+            and self.window_size_right is None
+        )
+
+    def _padded_tail_form(self) -> int:
+        """The ``TemplateParams.padded_tail_form`` of this plan: 0 off the eligible rendering; else the request (``padded_tail_form=``,
+        validated by ``check_support``) or the pick (``config_sm107.sm107_padded_tail_form_pick``: the default constant or the sweep seam)."""
+        if not self._padded_tail_form_eligible():
+            return 0
+        if self._device_cc != (10, 7):
+            return _sm100_padded_tail_form_pick(
+                self.flavor[0],
+                padded=True,
+                has_bias=self.bias_desc is not None,
+                has_kv_mask=False,
+                request=self.padded_tail_form,
+                tile_n=self._effective_tile_n(),
+            )
+        return _sm107_padded_tail_form_pick(
+            self.flavor[0],
+            padded=True,
+            has_bias=False,
+            has_kv_mask=False,
+            request=self.padded_tail_form,
+            tile_n=self._effective_tile_n(),
+        )
+
+    def _dead_subtile_quiet_eligible(self) -> bool:
+        """Whether this plan runs a rendering whose dead softmax sub-tile (no live row) can take the quiet body (``TemplateParams.dead_subtile_quiet``):
+        on the Rubin small tiles the one-batch-entry item without a bias (the quiet body there replicates the plain row mapping's barrier sequence,
+        none of the bias barriers); on the SM100 small tiles the -inf body (a bias or a kv_mask; the quiet body there carries the ring handshake),
+        off the d64 decode tile."""
+        if self._device_cc in _SM100_BIAS_CCS:
+            return (
+                not self._fp8
+                and self.flavor in _SM100_BIAS_D_SHAPES
+                and not self.thd
+                and not self.pack_gqa
+                and self.gate_desc is None
+                and (self.bias_desc is not None or self.kv_mask_desc is not None)
+                and not self._d64_decode_tile()
+            )
+        return (
+            self._device_cc == (10, 7)
+            and not self._fp8
+            and self.flavor in _SM107_F16_SMALL_D_SHAPES
+            and not self.thd
+            and not self.pack_gqa
+            and self.gate_desc is None
+            and self.bias_desc is None
+        )
+
+    def _dead_subtile_quiet(self) -> int:
+        """The ``TemplateParams.dead_subtile_quiet`` of this plan: 0 off the eligible rendering; else the request (``dead_subtile_quiet=``,
+        validated by ``check_support``) or the pick (``config_sm107.sm107_dead_subtile_quiet_pick``: the default constant or the sweep seam)."""
+        if not self._dead_subtile_quiet_eligible():
+            return 0
+        if self._device_cc != (10, 7):
+            return _sm100_dead_subtile_quiet_pick(
+                self.flavor[0],
+                has_bias=self.bias_desc is not None,
+                has_kv_mask=self.kv_mask_desc is not None,
+                request=self.dead_subtile_quiet,
+                s_q=int(self.q_desc.shape[2]),
+                cga=int(self.cga) if self.cga is not None else 1,
+                padded=bool(self.seq_kv_lens_present),
+                tile_n=self._effective_tile_n(),
+            )

@@ -818,12 +883,271 @@ def put(name, value):
     s.template = t
     # Every admitted dense template, including staged compact cores, owns
     # the native contract. The constructor validates its complete host ABI.
+    # One exception: the score side outputs and the resident-block arms (bias / kv_mask) bind through the python frame
+    # (``bind_dense`` below) -- the native binder's slot vocabulary predates their host slots (it copies the template's
+    # None / zero slots untouched), so a plan that requests them keeps ``native`` None and ``bind_dense`` fills the
+    # pointer / stride slots per call.
+    if s.has_score_max or s.has_score_sum_exp or s.has_bias or s.has_kv_mask:
+        s.native = None
+        return s
     from cudnn import _pybind_module
 
     s.native = _pybind_module._SdpaDenseBinder(s)
     return s
 
 
+# ---- The python-frame binding of the plans the native binder cannot bind (score side outputs, bias, kv_mask):
+# the role helpers below, ``_dense_lse``, ``bind_dense`` and ``bind_dense_split`` are the pre-native dense frame, kept for
+# exactly those plans (``build_dense_spec`` leaves their ``native`` None); every other dense plan binds natively.
+
+
+def _on_plan_device(spec, name: str, f: BufferFacts) -> None:
+    # one device rule for every bound role: a KNOWN producer device must be the plan's CUDA device
+    if f.device[0] != -1 and f.device != (_DLPACK_CUDA, spec.device_index):
+        raise ValueError(f"cudnn.sdpa: " + (f"{name} must be on CUDA device {spec.device_index} (this plan's); got DLPack device {f.device}"))
+
+
+def _bind_paged_kv(spec, frame: List[Any], ix: Dict[str, int], facts: Dict[str, Optional[BufferFacts]], k: BufferFacts, v: BufferFacts, b: int) -> int:
+    """Bind the page pools and tables of a paged launch; returns SKV = max_pages * page_size. Shared by
+    the THD and dense binders (one implementation of the paged domain)."""
+    # K/V are page pools (n_pages, page_size, KH, D) in the kernel's order: a permutation of the
+    # container's (n_pages, KH, page_size, D) strides; SKV = max_pages * page_size
+    bt, btv = facts.get("block_table"), facts.get("block_table_v")
+    if bt is None or btv is None:
+        raise ValueError(f"cudnn.sdpa: " + ("paged KV requires paged_attention_k_table / paged_attention_v_table buffers"))
+    if bt.dtype != "int32" or btv.dtype != "int32":
+        raise ValueError(f"cudnn.sdpa: " + ("the page tables must be int32"))
+    _on_plan_device(spec, "paged_attention_k_table", bt)
+    _on_plan_device(spec, "paged_attention_v_table", btv)
+
+    for name, table in (("paged_attention_k_table", bt), ("paged_attention_v_table", btv)):
+        if not table.ptr or table.ptr % _ALIGN_F32:
+            raise ValueError(f"cudnn.sdpa: {name} must have a non-null, 4-byte-aligned address")
+    try:
+        (tb, max_pages), table_strides = _paged_table_layout(bt.shape, bt.strides)
+    except ValueError as error:
+        raise ValueError(f"cudnn.sdpa: paged_attention_k_table {error}") from error
+    try:
+        (tbv, max_pages_v), table_strides_v = _paged_table_layout(btv.shape, btv.strides)
+    except ValueError as error:
+        raise ValueError(f"cudnn.sdpa: paged_attention_v_table {error}") from error
+    if tb < b or tbv < b:
+        raise ValueError(f"cudnn.sdpa: " + (f"the page tables describe {tb} / {tbv} sequences; this call runs {b}"))
+    if max_pages_v != max_pages:
+        raise ValueError("cudnn.sdpa: paged_attention_k_table and paged_attention_v_table must share max_pages")
+    if "table_v_strides" not in ix and table_strides_v != table_strides:
+        raise ValueError("cudnn.sdpa: this prepared host requires matching K/V table strides")
+    # Each table keeps its own observed storage bound and physical geometry.
+    for name, table, strides in (("k", bt, table_strides), ("v", btv, table_strides_v)):
+        need = (b - 1) * strides[0] + (max_pages - 1) * strides[1] + 1
+        if table.span >= 0 and table.span < need:
+            raise ValueError(f"cudnn.sdpa: paged_attention_{name}_table spans {table.span} elements; ({b}, {max_pages}) with strides {strides} needs {need}")
+    # the pools: (n_pages, KH, page_size, D) containers, head dim contiguous, one page count for K and V,
+    # and the in-page layout kind the artifact was compiled for (its TMA descriptors order (row, head) by it)
+    pool_strides = {}
+    for name, f, d in (("k", k, spec.d_qk), ("v", v, spec.d_v)):
+        try:
+            strides, need = _paged_pool_layout(f.shape, f.strides, _buffers.DTYPE_ITEMSIZE[f.dtype], spec.paged_hnd, spec.kh, spec.page_size, d)
+        except ValueError as error:
+            raise ValueError(f"cudnn.sdpa: {name}: {error}") from error
+        if f.span >= 0 and f.span < need:
+            raise ValueError(f"cudnn.sdpa: {name}: page pool spans {f.span} elements; its effective geometry needs {need}")
+        pool_strides[name] = strides
+    if int(k.shape[0]) != int(v.shape[0]):
+        raise ValueError(f"cudnn.sdpa: " + (f"K and V pools must hold the same number of pages; got {k.shape[0]} and {v.shape[0]}"))
+    t_kv = max_pages * spec.page_size
+    frame[ix["k_strides"]], frame[ix["v_strides"]] = pool_strides["k"], pool_strides["v"]
+    frame[ix["block_table_ptr"]], frame[ix["block_table_v_ptr"]] = bt.ptr, btv.ptr
+    frame[ix["table_strides"]] = (int(table_strides[0]), int(table_strides[1]))
+    if "table_v_strides" in ix:
+        frame[ix["table_v_strides"]] = (int(table_strides_v[0]), int(table_strides_v[1]))
+    frame[ix["n_pages"]] = int(k.shape[0])
+    return t_kv
+
+
+def _packed_role(spec: DenseLaunchSpec, facts: Dict[str, Optional[BufferFacts]], name: str, heads: int, d: int, expect: str, *, tma: bool):
+    """One PACKED (THD) operand of the ragged-Q leg -- the graph's (B, H, S_max, D) declaration or a
+    (T, H, D) buffer -- as ``(ptr, token_stride, head_stride, token_capacity)``.  The batch stride is
+    never read (every row base is a ragged offset); the token stride must cover the heads and, for a
+    TMA operand, be a 16-byte multiple; the capacity is the largest token whose row lies inside the
+    buffer's span (the THD contract: rows below it are caller-provided, rows at or past it TMA-clip)."""
+    f = facts.get(name)
+    if f is None:
+        raise ValueError(f"cudnn.sdpa: {name} is required")
+    if f.dtype != expect:
+        raise ValueError(f"cudnn.sdpa: {name}: runtime buffer dtype {f.dtype} does not match its declaration ({expect})")
+    _on_plan_device(spec, name, f)
+    width = _buffers.DTYPE_ITEMSIZE[expect]
+    if f.ptr % (_ALIGN_TMA if tma else width) != 0:
+        raise ValueError(f"cudnn.sdpa: {name}: runtime buffer base address must be {_ALIGN_TMA if tma else width}-byte aligned")
+    ts, hs, row = _packed_role_layout(tuple(f.shape), tuple(f.strides), heads, d, width, tma, name)
+    capacity = _capacity(f, (ts, hs, 1, row), name)
