+                + [
+                    (f"weights.{f}", getattr(weights, f))
+                    for f in ("w_in", "b_in", "norm_in_weight", "norm_in_bias", "norm_out_weight", "norm_out_bias", "p_out_weight", "g_out_weight", "b_out")
+                ]
+            )
+        else:
+            _autograd_decline([("x", x), ("mask", mask), ("out", out)])
+        # the PLAN's device first: its kernels are loaded on cuda:<device_index> and launched there -- tensors on another device would pass
+        # every shape check below and hand foreign pointers to kernels running on the wrong GPU
+        if self.device.type == "cuda" and (not isinstance(x, torch.Tensor) or x.device.type != "cuda" or x.device.index != self.device_index):
+            raise ValueError(
+                f"x lives on {getattr(x, 'device', None)}; this plan was declared on cuda:{self.device_index} and its kernels are loaded there "
+                "(declare and compile one plan per device)"
+            )
+        if not isinstance(x, torch.Tensor) or x.dtype != bf16 or not x.is_contiguous() or tuple(x.shape) != (b, n, n, c_z):
+            raise ValueError(
+                f"x must be a contiguous bf16 [{b}, {n}, {n}, {c_z}] tensor (the declaration), got {getattr(x, 'shape', None)} {getattr(x, 'dtype', None)}"
+            )
+        if not isinstance(out, torch.Tensor) or out.dtype != bf16 or not out.is_contiguous() or tuple(out.shape) != (b, n, n, c_z):
+            raise ValueError(f"out must be a contiguous bf16 [{b}, {n}, {n}, {c_z}] tensor, got {getattr(out, 'shape', None)} {getattr(out, 'dtype', None)}")
+        if self.has_mask:
+            if mask is None:
+                raise ValueError("this plan was compiled with has_mask=True; a bf16 [B, N, N] mask must be passed (no silent all-valid fallback)")
+            if mask.dtype != bf16 or not mask.is_contiguous() or tuple(mask.shape) != (b, n, n):
+                raise ValueError(f"mask must be a contiguous bf16 [{b}, {n}, {n}] tensor, got {tuple(mask.shape)} {mask.dtype}")
+        elif mask is not None:
+            raise ValueError("this plan was compiled with has_mask=False; mask must be None (compile a plan with has_mask=True to apply one)")
+        if not isinstance(weights, TriMulWeights):
+            raise TypeError("weights must be a TriMulWeights (prepare_weights(...)); the kernels take the interleaved layouts, prepared once")
+        if (weights.c_z, weights.c) != (c_z, c):
+            raise ValueError(f"weights were prepared for (c_z, c) = {(weights.c_z, weights.c)}, the plan for {(c_z, c)}")
+        if weights.has_in_bias != self.has_in_bias:
+            raise ValueError(f"this plan was compiled with has_in_bias={self.has_in_bias}; the weights carry an input bias: {weights.has_in_bias}")
+        if weights.has_out_bias != self.has_out_bias:
+            raise ValueError(f"this plan was compiled with has_out_bias={self.has_out_bias}; the weights carry an output bias: {weights.has_out_bias}")
+        if (
+            not isinstance(workspace, torch.Tensor)
+            or workspace.dtype != torch.uint8
+            or workspace.numel() < self.get_workspace_size()
+            or not workspace.is_contiguous()
+        ):
+            raise ValueError(f"workspace must be a contiguous uint8 tensor of at least get_workspace_size() = {self.get_workspace_size()} bytes")
+        for name, t in (("x", x), ("out", out), ("workspace", workspace), ("mask", mask)):
+            if t is not None and t.device != x.device:
+                raise ValueError(f"{name} must live on x's device {x.device}, got {t.device}")
+        if weights.device != x.device:
+            raise ValueError(f"weights must live on x's device {x.device}, got {weights.device}")
+        if workspace.data_ptr() % _WS_ALIGN:
+            raise ValueError(f"workspace must be {_WS_ALIGN}-byte aligned")
+        if out.data_ptr() == x.data_ptr():
+            raise ValueError("out must not alias x (the output stage reads x while it writes out)")
+
+    def _carve(self, workspace: torch.Tensor):
+        """``(plane_a, plane_b, y)`` views over the workspace (no allocation)."""
+        p = self.planes_shape
+        planes = workspace[: 2 * p[0] * p[1] * p[2] * p[3]].view(torch.bfloat16).view(*p)
+        yb = self._y_bytes()
+        y_off = self._planes_bytes() + self._slack_bytes()
+        y = workspace[y_off : y_off + yb][: 2 * self.y_shape[0] * self.y_shape[1] * self.y_shape[2]].view(torch.bfloat16).view(*self.y_shape)
+        return planes, planes[0], planes[1], y
+
+    def execute(self, x, mask, weights, out, workspace, current_stream: Optional[cuda.CUstream] = None) -> None:
+        """Launch K1, K2, K3 on ``current_stream`` (None = torch's current stream on the plan's device).  Validates, never converts or
+        allocates.  The launches run with the plan's device current (``torch.cuda.device`` -- a context switch, no synchronisation), so a
+        plan declared on ``cuda:1`` is served from any current device."""
+        if self._compiled_kernel is None:
+            raise RuntimeError("compile() must run before execute()")
+        self._check_execute_args(x, mask, weights, out, workspace)
+        stream = _stream_handle(current_stream, self.device)
+        with torch.cuda.device(self.device_index):
+            self._launch(x, mask, weights, out, workspace, stream)
+
+    def _launch(self, x, mask, weights, out, workspace, stream: int) -> None:
+        planes, plane_a, plane_b, y = self._carve(workspace)
+        b, n, c_z = self.batch, self.n_res, self.c_z
+        k1.run_trimul_proj(
+            self._plan_k1,
+            x,
+            weights.w_in,
+            planes,
+            weights.norm_in_weight,
+            weights.norm_in_bias,
+            bias_stacked=weights.b_in,
+            mask=mask,
+            stats=None,
+            stream=stream,
+            k_block=self.knobs.k_block,
+        )
+        a_v, b_v, y_v = k2.k2_operand_views(plane_a, plane_b, y, channels=self.c, batch=b, n_res=n, direction=self.direction)
+        bd = self._k2_binding
+        self._k2({bd.a_operands[0]: a_v, bd.b_operands[0]: b_v, bd.outputs[0]: y_v}, stream=stream)
+        k3.run_trimul_tail(
+            self._plan_k3,
+            y,
+            x,
+            weights.p_out_weight,
+            weights.g_out_weight,
+            out,
+            weights.norm_out_weight,
+            weights.norm_out_bias,
+            weights.norm_in_weight,
+            weights.norm_in_bias,
+            biases=weights.b_out,
+            stats=None,
+            residual=None,
+            stream=stream,
+            k_block=self.knobs.k_block,
+        )
+
+    def make_cuda_graph(self, x, mask, weights, out, workspace, *, warmup: int = 2) -> "torch.cuda.CUDAGraph":
+        """Capture the three launches for THESE buffers into one ``torch.cuda.CUDAGraph`` (replay = one graph launch per call; the
+        buffers' contents may change between replays, their addresses may not).  ``warmup`` eager calls run first on a side stream."""
+        side = torch.cuda.Stream(device=x.device)
+        side.wait_stream(torch.cuda.current_stream(x.device))
+        with torch.cuda.stream(side):
+            for _ in range(int(warmup)):
+                self.execute(x, mask, weights, out, workspace, current_stream=cuda.CUstream(side.cuda_stream))
+        torch.cuda.current_stream(x.device).wait_stream(side)
+        torch.cuda.synchronize(x.device)
+        graph = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
+        with torch.cuda.graph(graph, stream=side):
+            self.execute(x, mask, weights, out, workspace, current_stream=cuda.CUstream(side.cuda_stream))
+        return graph
+
+
+_K2_LOCK = threading.Lock()
+_K2_CACHE: Dict[Tuple[Any, ...], Any] = {}
+_SUBSTRATE_LOCK = threading.Lock()
+_SUBSTRATE_PLANS: Dict[Tuple[Any, int], Any] = {}
+
+
+def _substrate_plan_on(build, params, device_index: int, arch: str = "sm107"):
+    """One cute-compiled launchable of the K1 / K3 substrate per (parameter set, arch body, device).  A CuTe-DSL launchable is bound to the CUDA
+    context it was first loaded in -- a K1 launchable built on ``cuda:0`` fails on ``cuda:1`` with ``cudaErrorInvalidValue`` at launch, and
+    vice versa (measured on a two-GPU host) -- while the substrate's ``build_*`` cache is per parameter set only.  Under the plan's device:
+    when the substrate's cache fills NOW its launchable is bound here and is reused (the single-device case pays nothing extra); when it was
+    filled earlier -- by a plan on another device, or by a caller outside this API -- the same template module gets a second ``cute.compile``
+    for this device, cached per (params, device)."""
+    from cudnn.gemm.frost import ln_prologue
+
+    key = (params, str(arch), int(device_index))
+    with _SUBSTRATE_LOCK:
+        hit = _SUBSTRATE_PLANS.get(key)
+    if hit is not None:
+        return hit
+    with torch.cuda.device(device_index), _SUBSTRATE_LOCK:
+        before = ln_prologue.build_ln_dual_gemm.cache_info().currsize
+        base = build(params, arch)
+        built_here = ln_prologue.build_ln_dual_gemm.cache_info().currsize > before
+        plan = base if built_here else ln_prologue.LnDualGemmPlan(params=base.params, module=base.module, launch=base.module.compile.__wrapped__())
+        return _SUBSTRATE_PLANS.setdefault(key, plan)
+
+
+def _compile_contraction(cudnn_module, channels: int, batch: int, n_res: int, direction: str, tile: str, device_index: int):
+    """The compiled FROST GEMM instance of the contraction for ``(c * B, direction, tile, dtype, device)`` -- M / N / K are symbolic in the
+    kernel, the batch count is baked, so the cache key is the folded batch, not N.  Keyed on the PLAN's device (not the current one): the
+    caller enters ``torch.cuda.device(device_index)`` around the compile, so a plan for ``cuda:1`` never binds a module loaded on ``cuda:0``."""
+    from cudnn.gemm.frost.compiler import jit_from_cudnn_graph
+    from cudnn.gemm.frost.tile_config import by_name
+
+    index = int(device_index)
+    key = (channels * batch, direction, tile, "bf16", index)
+    with _K2_LOCK:
+        hit = _K2_CACHE.get(key)
+        if hit is not None:
+            return hit
+    graph = k2.contraction_graph(cudnn_module, channels, n_res, direction, batch=batch, padded=True)
+    compiled = jit_from_cudnn_graph(graph, config=by_name(tile))
+    with _K2_LOCK:
+        return _K2_CACHE.setdefault(key, compiled)
+
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# The drop-in function (cuEquivariance's signature)
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+_PLAN_LOCK = threading.Lock()
+_PLANS: Dict[Tuple[Any, ...], TriangleMultiplicativeUpdateFwd] = {}
+_WEIGHTS: "OrderedDict[Tuple[Any, ...], Tuple[TriMulWeights, tuple]]" = OrderedDict()
+_WEIGHTS_MAX = 8
+
+_PRECISION_DEFAULT = ("NONE", "DEFAULT")
+_PRECISION_BF16 = ("BF16", "BFLOAT16")
+
+
+def _parse_precision(precision) -> str:
+    """cuEquivariance's ``precision`` spellings -> ``"default"`` (bf16 inputs required) or ``"bfloat16"`` (cast wider inputs); the
+    rest (``"mxfp8"``, ``"ieee"``, ``"tf32"``, ...) are typed declines."""
+    if precision is None:
+        return "default"
+    name = None
+    if isinstance(precision, str):
+        name = precision.upper()
+    elif isinstance(precision, int) and not isinstance(precision, bool):
+        name = {-1: "NONE", 0: "DEFAULT", 5: "BFLOAT16", 4: "MXFP8", 3: "IEEE", 1: "TF32", 2: "TF32X3"}.get(precision, str(precision))
+    elif hasattr(precision, "name"):
+        name = str(precision.name).upper()
+    else:
+        raise ValueError(f"precision must be None, a string or a cuEquivariance Precision, got {type(precision).__name__}")
+    if name in _PRECISION_DEFAULT:
+        return "default"
+    if name in _PRECISION_BF16:
+        return "bfloat16"
+    if name == "MXFP8":
+        raise NotImplementedError("precision='mxfp8' (block-scaled a / b operands) is not served by triangle_multiplicative_update yet")
+    raise NotImplementedError(f"precision={precision!r} is not served by triangle_multiplicative_update (bf16 arithmetic only: None / 'default' / 'bfloat16')")
+
+
+def _tensor_identity(t: Optional[torch.Tensor]):
+    if t is None:
+        return None
+    return (t.data_ptr(), t.storage_offset(), tuple(t.shape), tuple(t.stride()), t.dtype, str(t.device), t._version)
+
+
+def _cached_weights(params: tuple, cast: bool) -> TriMulWeights:
+    """One prepared weight set per PARAMETER IDENTITY (address, shape, strides, dtype, device and torch's in-place version counter
+    of each of the twelve tensors); the entry keeps a reference to the source tensors so an address cannot be recycled under it.
+    A bounded LRU: a model switches parameter sets rarely, a training loop bumps the version counter and misses (one re-interleave)."""
+    key = (cast,) + tuple(_tensor_identity(t) for t in params)
+    with _PLAN_LOCK:
+        hit = _WEIGHTS.get(key)
+        if hit is not None:
+            _WEIGHTS.move_to_end(key)
+            return hit[0]
+    prepared = prepare_weights(*params, cast_to_bf16=cast)
+    with _PLAN_LOCK:
+        _WEIGHTS[key] = (prepared, tuple(t for t in params if t is not None))
+        _WEIGHTS.move_to_end(key)
+        while len(_WEIGHTS) > _WEIGHTS_MAX:
+            _WEIGHTS.popitem(last=False)
+    return prepared
+
+
+def _cached_plan(x: torch.Tensor, direction: str, c: int, has_mask: bool, has_in_bias: bool, has_out_bias: bool, eps: float) -> TriangleMultiplicativeUpdateFwd:
+    key = (tuple(x.shape), x.dtype, str(x.device), direction, int(c), bool(has_mask), bool(has_in_bias), bool(has_out_bias), float(eps))
+    with _PLAN_LOCK:
+        plan = _PLANS.get(key)
+    if plan is not None:
+        return plan
+    plan = TriangleMultiplicativeUpdateFwd(x, direction, c_hidden=c, has_mask=has_mask, has_in_bias=has_in_bias, has_out_bias=has_out_bias, eps=eps)
+    plan.check_support()
+    plan.compile()
+    with _PLAN_LOCK:
+        return _PLANS.setdefault(key, plan)
+
+
+def triangle_multiplicative_update(
+    x: torch.Tensor,
+    direction: str = "outgoing",
+    mask: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None,
+    norm_in_weight: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None,
+    norm_in_bias: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None,
+    p_in_weight: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None,
+    p_in_bias: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None,
+    g_in_weight: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None,
+    g_in_bias: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None,
+    norm_out_weight: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None,
+    norm_out_bias: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None,
+    p_out_weight: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None,
+    p_out_bias: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None,
+    g_out_weight: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None,
+    g_out_bias: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None,
+    eps: float = 1e-5,
+    precision=None,
+    *,
+    out: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None,
+    stream=None,
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """The triangle multiplicative update of ``x`` (``[B, N, N, c_z]`` or ``[N, N, c_z]`` bf16) -- cuEquivariance's signature
+    (``cuequivariance_ops_torch.triangle_multiplicative_update``, 0.12.0) with two keyword-only additions: ``out`` (write into this
+    bf16 tensor instead of allocating) and ``stream`` (a raw CUDA stream handle the allocations and launches are ordered on; None = torch's
+    current stream).  Returns the update (the caller adds the residual), shaped like ``x``.
+
+    Differences from cuEquivariance, all typed: the eight weights are REQUIRED (no implicit random initialisation); ``precision`` is
+    None / ``'default'`` (bf16 inputs required) or ``'bfloat16'`` (wider inputs cast once per call, as cuEquivariance does), ``'mxfp8'`` and
+    the IEEE / TF32 modes decline; a non-contiguous ``x`` declines; autograd is not registered yet, so under grad mode an input or
+    parameter with ``requires_grad`` is a typed decline (``NotImplementedError``), never a tensor without a ``grad_fn`` -- call under
+    ``torch.no_grad()`` or detach for inference.  A mask of any real or bool dtype is cast once per call to the kernels' bf16 ``[B, N, N]`` (no copy when
+    it already is).  One compiled plan per (shape, direction, flags) and one prepared weight set per parameter identity are cached in
+    the process; warm a shape before capturing a CUDA graph around this call.
+    """
+    from cudnn._torch_stream import stream_context
+
+    if direction not in DIRECTIONS:
+        raise ValueError(f"direction must be one of {DIRECTIONS}, got {direction!r}")
+    mode = _parse_precision(precision)
+    cast = mode == "bfloat16"
+    if not isinstance(x, torch.Tensor):
+        raise TypeError(f"x must be a torch.Tensor, got {type(x).__name__}")
+    squeeze = x.ndim == 3
+    x4 = x.unsqueeze(0) if squeeze else x
+    if x4.ndim != 4 or x4.shape[1] != x4.shape[2]:
+        raise ValueError(f"x must be [B, N, N, c_z] or [N, N, c_z], got {tuple(x.shape)}")
+    if p_in_weight is None or p_in_weight.ndim != 2 or p_in_weight.shape[0] % 2:
+        raise ValueError("p_in_weight is required and must be [2 c, c_z] (rows [a; b])")
+    for name, w in (
+        ("norm_in_weight", norm_in_weight),
+        ("norm_in_bias", norm_in_bias),
+        ("g_in_weight", g_in_weight),
+        ("norm_out_weight", norm_out_weight),
+        ("norm_out_bias", norm_out_bias),
+        ("p_out_weight", p_out_weight),
+        ("g_out_weight", g_out_weight),
+    ):
+        if w is None:
+            raise ValueError(f"{name} is required (this API never initialises parameters implicitly)")
+    c = int(p_in_weight.shape[0]) // 2
+    _autograd_decline(
+        [
+            ("x", x),
+            ("mask", mask),
+            ("norm_in_weight", norm_in_weight),
+            ("norm_in_bias", norm_in_bias),
+            ("p_in_weight", p_in_weight),
+            ("p_in_bias", p_in_bias),
+            ("g_in_weight", g_in_weight),
+            ("g_in_bias", g_in_bias),
+            ("norm_out_weight", norm_out_weight),
+            ("norm_out_bias", norm_out_bias),
+            ("p_out_weight", p_out_weight),
+            ("p_out_bias", p_out_bias),
+            ("g_out_weight", g_out_weight),
+            ("g_out_bias", g_out_bias),
+            ("out", out),
+        ]
+    )
+    device = x4.device
+    with stream_context(stream, device):
+        if x4.dtype != torch.bfloat16:
+            if not cast:
+                raise NotImplementedError(
+                    f"triangle_multiplicative_update serves bf16 pair representations only (got {x4.dtype}); pass precision='bfloat16' to cast like cuEquivariance"
+                )
+            x4 = x4.to(torch.bfloat16)
+        if not x4.is_contiguous():
+            raise ValueError("x must be contiguous ([B, N, N, c_z] row-major); the kernels read it natively and never repack")
+        batch, n_res = int(x4.shape[0]), int(x4.shape[1])
+        m = None
+        if mask is not None:
+            m = mask.unsqueeze(0) if mask.ndim == 2 else mask
+            if m.ndim != 3 or tuple(m.shape) != (batch, n_res, n_res):
+                raise ValueError(f"mask must be [B, N, N] = {(batch, n_res, n_res)} (or [N, N] for B = 1), got {tuple(mask.shape)}")
+            if m.dtype != torch.bfloat16:
+                m = m.to(torch.bfloat16)  # bool / fp32 masks: cast once per call (cuEquivariance's path too)
+            if not m.is_contiguous():
+                m = m.contiguous()
+        has_in_bias = p_in_bias is not None or g_in_bias is not None
+        has_out_bias = p_out_bias is not None or g_out_bias is not None
+        # the plan first: its typed declines (width, N, direction, arch) must fire before any parameter is touched
+        plan = _cached_plan(x4, direction, c, m is not None, has_in_bias, has_out_bias, float(eps))
+        weights = _cached_weights(
+            (
+                norm_in_weight,
+                norm_in_bias,
+                p_in_weight,
+                p_in_bias,
+                g_in_weight,
+                g_in_bias,
+                norm_out_weight,
+                norm_out_bias,
+                p_out_weight,
+                p_out_bias,
+                g_out_weight,
+                g_out_bias,
+            ),
+            cast,
+        )
+        if out is None:
+            out4 = torch.empty_like(x4)
+        else:
+            out4 = out.unsqueeze(0) if out.ndim == 3 else out
+        workspace = torch.empty(plan.get_workspace_size(), dtype=torch.uint8, device=device)
+        plan.execute(x4, m, weights, out4, workspace, current_stream=cuda.CUstream(_stream_handle(stream, device)))
+    return out4.squeeze(0) if squeeze else out4

+        raise ValueError(f"cudnn.sdpa: " + ("the page tables must be int32"))

+    _on_plan_device(spec, "paged_attention_v_table", btv)
+
+    for name, table in (("paged_attention_k_table", bt), ("paged_attention_v_table", btv)):
+        if not table.ptr or table.ptr % _ALIGN_F32:
+            raise ValueError(f"cudnn.sdpa: {name} must have a non-null, 4-byte-aligned address")
+    try:
+        (tb, max_pages), table_strides = _paged_table_layout(bt.shape, bt.strides)
+    except ValueError as error:
+        raise ValueError(f"cudnn.sdpa: paged_attention_k_table {error}") from error
+    try:
+        (tbv, max_pages_v), table_strides_v = _paged_table_layout(btv.shape, btv.strides)
+    except ValueError as error:
+        raise ValueError(f"cudnn.sdpa: paged_attention_v_table {error}") from error
+    if tb < b or tbv < b:
+        raise ValueError(f"cudnn.sdpa: " + (f"the page tables describe {tb} / {tbv} sequences; this call runs {b}"))
+    if max_pages_v != max_pages:
+        raise ValueError("cudnn.sdpa: paged_attention_k_table and paged_attention_v_table must share max_pages")
+    if "table_v_strides" not in ix and table_strides_v != table_strides:
+        raise ValueError("cudnn.sdpa: this prepared host requires matching K/V table strides")
+    # Each table keeps its own observed storage bound and physical geometry.
+    for name, table, strides in (("k", bt, table_strides), ("v", btv, table_strides_v)):
+        need = (b - 1) * strides[0] + (max_pages - 1) * strides[1] + 1
+        if table.span >= 0 and table.span < need:
+            raise ValueError(f"cudnn.sdpa: paged_attention_{name}_table spans {table.span} elements; ({b}, {max_pages}) with strides {strides} needs {need}")
+    # the pools: (n_pages, KH, page_size, D) containers, head dim contiguous, one page count for K and V,
+    # and the in-page layout kind the artifact was compiled for (its TMA descriptors order (row, head) by it)
+    pool_strides = {}
+    for name, f, d in (("k", k, spec.d_qk), ("v", v, spec.d_v)):
+        try:
+            strides, need = _paged_pool_layout(f.shape, f.strides, _buffers.DTYPE_ITEMSIZE[f.dtype], spec.paged_hnd, spec.kh, spec.page_size, d)
+        except ValueError as error:
+            raise ValueError(f"cudnn.sdpa: {name}: {error}") from error
+        if f.span >= 0 and f.span < need:
+            raise ValueError(f"cudnn.sdpa: {name}: page pool spans {f.span} elements; its effective geometry needs {need}")
+        pool_strides[name] = strides
+    if int(k.shape[0]) != int(v.shape[0]):
+        raise ValueError(f"cudnn.sdpa: " + (f"K and V pools must hold the same number of pages; got {k.shape[0]} and {v.shape[0]}"))
+    t_kv = max_pages * spec.page_size
+    frame[ix["k_strides"]], frame[ix["v_strides"]] = pool_strides["k"], pool_strides["v"]
+    frame[ix["block_table_ptr"]], frame[ix["block_table_v_ptr"]] = bt.ptr, btv.ptr
+    frame[ix["table_strides"]] = (int(table_strides[0]), int(table_strides[1]))
+    if "table_v_strides" in ix:
+        frame[ix["table_v_strides"]] = (int(table_strides_v[0]), int(table_strides_v[1]))
+    frame[ix["n_pages"]] = int(k.shape[0])
+    return t_kv
+
+
+def _packed_role(spec: DenseLaunchSpec, facts: Dict[str, Optional[BufferFacts]], name: str, heads: int, d: int, expect: str, *, tma: bool):
+    """One PACKED (THD) operand of the ragged-Q leg -- the graph's (B, H, S_max, D) declaration or a
+    (T, H, D) buffer -- as ``(ptr, token_stride, head_stride, token_capacity)``.  The batch stride is
+    never read (every row base is a ragged offset); the token stride must cover the heads and, for a
+    TMA operand, be a 16-byte multiple; the capacity is the largest token whose row lies inside the
+    buffer's span (the THD contract: rows below it are caller-provided, rows at or past it TMA-clip)."""
+    f = facts.get(name)
+    if f is None:
+        raise ValueError(f"cudnn.sdpa: {name} is required")
+    if f.dtype != expect:
+        raise ValueError(f"cudnn.sdpa: {name}: runtime buffer dtype {f.dtype} does not match its declaration ({expect})")
+    _on_plan_device(spec, name, f)
+    width = _buffers.DTYPE_ITEMSIZE[expect]
+    if f.ptr % (_ALIGN_TMA if tma else width) != 0:
+        raise ValueError(f"cudnn.sdpa: {name}: runtime buffer base address must be {_ALIGN_TMA if tma else width}-byte aligned")
+    ts, hs, row = _packed_role_layout(tuple(f.shape), tuple(f.strides), heads, d, width, tma, name)
+    capacity = _capacity(f, (ts, hs, 1, row), name)

Supplemental native validation of `2816e8dccf6f6b3ba2564feb6c5d2810478d54b4`, following the [earlier review](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1607#pullrequestreview-5538012984).

On native SM100 (148 SMs), with Torch 2.14.1 and CuTe DSL 4.8, **14 TriMul tests passed, zero skipped**: eight FP64-reference cases covering both directions, padding/tails, biases and widths 128/256; hand-chained equivalence; warm plan/weight caches; execute allocation/synchronization checks; changed-input CUDA-graph replay; and performance-knob equivalence. Source and the matching built FE extension were pinned to the reviewed head. This supplements the earlier compilation failure on the admitted DSL 4.7 floor; it does not resolve that compatibility finding.

**The existing partial-overlap concern is now reproduced on hardware.** For [CodeRabbit's comment](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1607#discussion_r4286436097), I used contiguous BF16 `[1, 512, 512, 128]` input/output views over one sufficiently large allocation, with `out` beginning halfway through `x`. Their pointers differ, so `_check_execute_args` accepts them. Compared with disjoint execution on identical inputs, all three trials produced **16,710,464 differing elements, max absolute error 2.560546875**. Disjoint-output controls were bitwise identical to baseline. Smaller N=128 and shorter offsets passed, so those alone would miss the inter-tile hazard. Please reject intersecting byte ranges before any launch; pointer inequality is insufficient. This is a narrow caller-supplied-buffer correctness issue, not evidence of failure for the disjoint cases above.

The earlier high-risk P1 findings (negative-scale additive-bias handling and the released DSL dependency floor) remain present at this head and should be addressed before merging. No approval or CI trigger from this supplement. Broader kernel review remains incomplete; native SM103/SM107 and performance are not qualified here. The attempted SM107 run stopped before kernel execution because the available compiler environment lacks the required architecture support.

Thank you for your contribution!

Codex bot review — model `gpt-6-astra`.

<!-- codex-fe-ci:v1:1607:2816e8dccf6f6b3ba2564feb6c5d2810478d54b4:native-validation-sm100-trimul-dsl48 -->

Four follow-up commits on this branch since the last push (develop merged at `8dc297a38`), plus one formatting-only commit:

**Test cleanup -- "keep only the critical ones".** The 22 new test modules go from 2125 cells to 1130 (-47 %); their GPU cells from 1124 to 454 (-60 %: cc 10.7 797 -> 294, cc 10.0 181 -> 74). What stays: every public accept / reject contract, one numerics oracle per shipped kernel body / knob default per form and dtype, every degenerate-input and invariant pin, every regression test of a bug fixed on the branch, every engine-row / capability / heuristics pin, and every rendering byte pin once, in the module that owns the record (no md5 record moved). What goes: geometry twins of byte-pinned bodies, fp16 twins beyond the degenerate trio, research seams and rejected arms (`test_sdpa_stages_kv_sm107.py` and `test_sdpa_tile_m_sm107.py` are removed with them), duplicate handshake / bitwise repeats. Eight cells the review found missing were added (the N1 regression below, a knob-less run of each shipped default body, two shipped-rendering spill pins, a bias-less barrier-table pin, a decode-tile backstop, a typed decline naming the served bias flavors). The trimul API module is renamed `test_trimul_api.py` so a whole-tree session no longer drops one of two `test_api.py` basenames. The K2 operand-views contract pin (`k2_operand_views` + the `k2_slack_bytes` over-read guard) is restored in `test_contraction_graph.py` after the cleanup dropped it as a duplicate of a pin on a different function. Three tests were renamed with equivalent content (`test_cfg_field_is_appended`, `test_sm107_ln_once_block_item_fold_rendering_spill_pin`, `test_direction_and_the_padded_incoming_tail_are_validated`); the two research seams `_STAGES_KV_OVERRIDE_FOR_SWEEPS` / `_TILE_M_OVERRIDE_FOR_SWEEPS` stay in `config_sm107.py` without a test.

**N1 fix (sm100 small tiles).** The quiet dead sub-tile body arrives `mb_bmm2_ready` without writing P, so BMM2 multiplied the S slot's residue; the epilogue folded the trim into the scale (`residue * 0 = NaN`), and under per-batch Q lengths with bottom-right causal a dead-but-stored sub-tile's rows could carry non-finite values. The epilogue now selects the trimmed rows to zero after the scale (`vec_select_zero`, a new `tile_dsl` primitive). Detector module `test_sdpa_dead_rows_sm100.py` (14 cells): RED 6 failed on the previous tree, GREEN 13 passed / 1 arch-skip on cc 10.0; the bias module's twin cell loses its strict xfail. Renderings of every `SEQ_Q_LENS_PRESENT` plan of that file change (the select itself); every other rendering is byte-identical.

**d128 prefill host entries (sm107 + sm100).** The appended score / bias / kv_mask host slots carried tuple defaults; the compiled-plan cache records a host's calling convention only from JSON-plain defaults, so it never persisted the d128 host and every process re-JIT'd it -- the staged artifact reload test failed on cc 10.7. The defaults are gone (every slot is explicit; the traced code and the rendering pins are unchanged), `test_sm107_half_split_direct_template_stats_base` reads the slot list off the host signature, and a host pin asserts record-reproducible defaults for every f16 flavor of both arch trees.

**Gates at the head** (every log attests the import path and device): host collection of the 27 modules 2786 cells / 0 errors; host, all tiers (every SASS and md5 pin rendered): **1896 passed / 890 skipped / 0 failed in 28 min 24 s, exit 0** (= 2786; the cleanup head's 1880 / 883 + the 16 new host cells and the 7 new device-gated cells; every skip a device-class gate, no nvdisasm / SASS / md5 skip); cc 10.7: **320 passed / 0 skipped in 738.65 s** (= the cleanup's 320) (bias / additive / head_dim), **1463 passed / 76 skipped in 1117.86 s** (= the cleanup's 1463 / 76; the skips = the cc 10.0-only cells of bias_sm100 / small_d_sm100 and two SM100 heuristics cells) (16 sdpa modules), **256 passed / 2 skipped in 748.03 s** (= the cleanup's 255 + the restored K2 pin; the skips = 'this device IS the served arch' and the two-GPU cell; the committed G8 cell `test_return_aux_is_a_typed_decline_quoting_the_engine` ran and passed here -- its first recorded run at committed content, VERIFY F1) (6 triangle modules), **638 passed / 17 skipped / 0 failed in 43 min 47 s** (= the cleanup's 627 + the 3 fixed cells + the 8 new host pins; the 17 skips = 'SM107 half split-KV remains unsupported', as before) (`test_sdpa_fwd_dsl_sm107.py`, the three previously failing cells included), the detector's cc 10.7 cells **8 passed / 6 skipped in 27.95 s** (the 7 host pins + the Rubin twin cell; the 6 cc 10.0 / 10.3 cells skip); cc 10.0: `test_sdpa_bias_sm100.py` **82 passed in 194.02 s**, 0 skipped -- the un-xfailed N1 cell among them, `test_sdpa_small_d_sm100.py` **52 passed in 132.41 s**, `test_sdpa_fwd_score_stats.py` **36 passed in 226.12 s** (every sm_100a / sm_107a md5 record pin and the score-arm SASS pins included; the comparison-plan pin holds on 152 SMs) (every sm_100a / sm_107a md5 pin), `test_sdpa_fwd_dsl_sm100.py` padded / bottom-right **109 passed in 280.54 s** (15 warnings = the DSL deprecation notice from the d512 file, as before) and its staged-reload cells **4 passed in 586.55 s** (`[128-128]`, `[192-128]`, `[256-256]`, `[512-512]`), `test_sdpa_dead_rows_sm100.py` **13 passed / 1 skipped in 36.39 s** (the skip = the Rubin twin cell), the 6 triangle modules **222 passed / 36 skipped in 1001.98 s** (the cleanup's 221 + the restored K2 pin; the skips = the triangle-attention Rubin-only gates and the two-GPU cell); black clean; no new lint warning.

Also in this push: a formatting-only commit (`black -l 160` on the four files the pre-commit hook reformats; black verified the syntax tree unchanged). The `\.` escape at `test_tile_dsl_release_arrive.py:165` is inside a raw string already (no SyntaxWarning on Python 3.12). Known, unchanged: the runtime `api_index` check needs `jax` in the venv.

Merged `develop` at f0fa620e2 into the branch (one conflict, in `sm107/prefill_d128_f16.py`: the branch's d-flavor factory dispatch and #1627's `dual_kv_stream` load-time guard both edit the same anchor line; the merge keeps both, dispatch then guard, as the sm100 sibling already reads). No rendering record was re-pinned: the merge gate re-rendered every arm of the six d128 md5 records (38 pins, sm_100a and sm_107a) byte-identical, since #1627's hunk in that kernel is a host-side record check that never reaches the traced code. Gates at the merge head, with the extension pair rebuilt for it on both architectures: host collection 2789 cells / 0 errors and all host tiers 1899 passed / 890 skipped / 0 failed in 28 min 05 s; cc 10.7 `test_sdpa_fwd_dsl_sm107.py` whole 638 passed / 17 skipped in 42 min 08 s (the skips: the unsupported half split-KV form, as before), the seven d128-file bias / head-dim modules 538 passed / 0 skipped in 22 min 39 s, the dead-rows and release-arrive modules 8 passed / 6 arch-skipped / 10 passed, the remaining sdpa modules 1238 passed / 76 arch-skipped in 7 min 09 s; cc 10.0 `test_sdpa_bias_sm100.py` 82 passed, `test_sdpa_small_d_sm100.py` 52 passed, `test_sdpa_fwd_score_stats.py` 36 passed (every sm_100a / sm_107a md5 pin included), `test_sdpa_dead_rows_sm100.py` 13 passed / 1 arch-skipped, `test_sdpa_fwd_dsl_sm100.py` padded / bottom-right 109 passed; black and the added-lines lint clean.

Merged `develop` at eaace52aa (#1680, the Rubin decode levers) into the branch: merge commit `e802a6d21` (parents `f73dffdb8`, the previous head, and `eaace52aa`; 45 files auto-merged, 3 conflicts, each resolved keeping both sides in full):

- `python/cudnn/sdpa/fwd/api_dsl.py`: the public constructor's appended tail now reads `..., ragged_offsets_int64, decode_q_tile_max, use_pdl` (develop's two released parameters stay in their released positions) followed by this branch's eleven (`sample_score_max` .. `softmax_wgs`); in `compile()`, develop's `use_pdl` decline comes first, then this branch's two `has_score_max` / `has_bias` backstops (disjoint predicates, base-first order).
- `python/cudnn/sdpa/fwd/engines.py`: develop's Amax_S deprecation warning (`_warn_amax_s_declared_once`) and this branch's `_resident_arm_layout_decline` / `_bias_arm_decline` are all kept as module-level definitions, develop's first; `mismatch()` carries develop's two `d256_decode_tile_served` sites and this branch's `_bias_arm_decline` site.
- `test/python/sdpa/frost/test_sdpa_fwd_dsl_sm107.py`: the signature-tail pin lists develop's `decode_q_tile_max`, `use_pdl` and then this branch's eleven names, i.e. the merged signature, with develop's two default pins kept. The branch's own adjacency pin in `test_sdpa_fwd_api_contract.py` (not a git conflict) was updated to the same order.

### P1-1 — Use the effective positive scale when binding additive bias — fixed in 9cc57699a (tests 0312afcb1)

**Fix.** `build_dense_spec`'s dense template derives both per-score constants from one `effective_scale` (`-scale` when the plan is negated): `inv_scale_softmax = 1 / effective_scale` and `scale_softmax_log2 = effective_scale * log2 e`, so they cannot diverge again; the SM90 natural-units `scale_softmax` keeps the caller's signed value. The graph route (`PreparedDenseLaunch.execute` → `bind_dense` → `spec.frame()`) copies the template per call, which is why it carried the signed `1 / scale`; the standalone adapter re-derived the slot from `|scale|` per call and was right (its override is a no-op now). Kernels untouched: every consumer adds `bias * inv_scale` to the raw score before the scale multiply (`bias_fma_chunk`, `additive_vec_fma_chunk`, and the upper-bound row max), so the sign is the host's contract. The THD template's neutral slot is never read (the d128 family validator refuses the bias / kv_mask arms on THD renderings); SM120 has no such slot; SM80 / SM90 have no `negate_scores`.

**RED on `9af6a861a`** (your recipe through the public graph route: zero Q / K, S 128, D 32, bf16, +2 on the first 64 keys / −2 on the rest as the resident bias block and as the additive `kv_mask` vector, V +1 / −1, `attn_scale` ±0.125): the two negative-scale cells read O = −tanh(2) against the +0.9640 oracle — `Mismatched elements: 8192 / 8192, Greatest absolute difference 1.9288713` on a GB200 class device (cc 10.0, 152 SMs; your number) and `1.9249651` on Rubin (cc 10.7, 204 SMs); the positive controls pass. The host template pin reads `inv_scale_softmax = -8.0` where `+8.0` (= 1 / |−0.125|) is required, for the sm100 and the sm107 host alike. 4 failed / 4 passed of the 8 cells that run on each device class.

**GREEN after the fix:** 8 passed / 0 failed on each device class (bias and additive-mask forms, both signs; the two-launch identity held in every cell), the host pin 4 / 4; at `e0a9f3bf8` the same cells pass inside the full-module runs listed at the end.

**Tests added.** `test_sdpa_bias_sm107.py::test_signed_attn_scale_keeps_the_additive_arms_sign[{positive,negative}_scale-{bias,additive_kv_mask}]` and `test_sdpa_bias_sm100.py::test_signed_attn_scale_keeps_the_additive_arms_sign_on_sm100[...]` (the public graph route, the shared fp64 oracle at the unchanged tolerances, the closed form tanh(2), and "not close to the negated oracle"), plus the device-free pin `test_prepared_dense_template_binds_the_additive_arms_inverse_scale_at_the_effective_magnitude[{positive,negative}_scale-{sm100,sm107}]`, which reads the template `build_dense_spec` writes and asserts `inv_scale_softmax == 1 / |scale|` and `scale_softmax_log2 == |scale| log2 e` on both signs.
